s5aa9e3310d.title: Context Scaling: A New Frontier of AI Scaling
s5aa9e3310d.description: arXiv:2611.33160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many failures of deployed AI arise not from weak inference but from a mismatch between the state a task depends on and the context available when the system acts. Relevant user state, repository revisions, tool traces, sensor readings, or environment changes may be unavailable, distorted, or poorly selected. We call the effort to reduce this bottleneck context scaling. We frame a model as $P_\theta(d\mid c)$ within a system governed by three budgets: training $B_\theta$, decision-time $B_d$, and context-infrastructure $B_c$. s5aa9e3310d.summary: An arXiv paper proposes "context scaling," framing deployed AI failures as mismatches between task-relevant state and the context available at decision time.
s5aa9e3310d.why: It suggests context infrastructure, not just training or inference compute, may limit deployed AI systems and deserves budgeting alongside them.

s3965806fbc.title: Constraint-Aware Test-Time Scoring for LLM and VLM Candidate Selection
s3965806fbc.description: arXiv:2611.33161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When an LLM or VLM produces several candidate answers, picking the best one usually relies on the model's own confidence, a learned judge model, or a domain check. Each has a known weakness: an answer can be fluent but insecure, mathematically plausible but physically infeasible, or rated highly by a judge while quietly breaking a task requirement. We propose a scoring framework that combines a small set of hard checks every answer must pass with a wider set of softer checks whose scores are blended into one number per candidate. s3965806fbc.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a test-time scoring framework that selects LLM and VLM candidate answers using hard checks plus blended softer checks.
s3965806fbc.why: Engineers choosing among model outputs could use explicit constraint checks rather than relying only on model confidence or a judge model.

sbe1cc5587b.title: AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics
sbe1cc5587b.description: arXiv:2611.33165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems are increasingly capable of producing machine-checked Lean proofs of advanced mathematical results. Real mathematical formalization, however, is not isolated theorem proving: it requires building the definitions and intermediate lemmas that connect a result to a formal library. Existing evaluations often provide isolated theorem statements in settings where much of this supporting theory is already available in Mathlib. We introduce AutoformBench, a benchmark of 341 Lean 4 formalization tasks drawn from 24 advanced mathematical sources. sbe1cc5587b.summary: An arXiv paper introduces AutoformBench, a benchmark of 341 Lean 4 tasks testing whether models can build supporting definitions and lemmas for advanced mathematics.
sbe1cc5587b.why: It tests formalization beyond isolated theorem proving, which is closer to how real formal math libraries are built.

sc8682f0486.title: General-Purpose Decision Models for AI Configuration Tuning
sc8682f0486.description: arXiv:2611.33190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI configuration tuning searches for settings that improve the performance of AI systems under a limited budget. Existing tuners use different sampling and search policies, making the choice of decision strategy central to both tuning quality and cost. We investigate whether general-purpose decision models can guide tuning, using Jev as a deployed representative that returns structured choices and numeric scores across diverse tasks. To assess where it helps, we compare its use as an optimizer, performance predictor, and region guider against conventional methods and a large language model (LLM) on eight AI tuning tasks. sc8682f0486.summary: An arXiv paper investigates whether a general-purpose decision model, Jev, can guide AI configuration tuning as an optimizer, performance predictor, or region guider.
sc8682f0486.why: If general decision models can match specialized tuners, teams may cut the cost of tuning AI system settings under limited budgets.

sef0eeffeb9.title: What, Who, and When: Structured Harm Assessment for Mental Health Safety via Short Reasoning
sef0eeffeb9.description: arXiv:2611.33263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing use of large language models (LLMs) for mental health support raises important safety concerns. Existing guard models primarily identify categories of harmful content, often overlooking the context needed to determine an appropriate response. We introduce a clinically grounded taxonomy that characterizes harm along three dimensions: what the harm is, who is involved, and when it occurs. It further separates harm characterization from intervention decisions, thus enabling safety policies to be specified outside the model weights through explicit, clinician-curated instructions that can be updated and audited. sef0eeffeb9.summary: An arXiv paper introduces a clinically grounded taxonomy for assessing LLM mental health harms along what, who, and when dimensions, separate from intervention decisions.
sef0eeffeb9.why: Separating harm characterization from intervention policy lets teams specify safety rules outside model weights for mental health applications.

s63908ad4c4.title: Certify What You Plant: Shortcut-Free Proof Depth in Logical Reasoning Data
s63908ad4c4.description: arXiv:2611.33303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Procedurally generated logic problems are used to both evaluate and train reasoning in language models. Their difficulty is usually set by planting a proof, that is, by sampling a proof of the desired depth and stating its premises as the problem. However, a planted proof is only one possible proof. A problem can also have shorter proofs, or several unrelated ones, and its stated depth then overstates what solving it requires. We measure what a problem actually requires, relative to a stated set of inference rules. For each problem, we compute the steps every proof must make, the shortest proof, the number of minimal proofs and the indispensable premises, and export certificates that an independent checker verifies. s63908ad4c4.summary: An arXiv paper shows that planted proofs can overstate the true depth of procedurally generated logic problems, and proposes measuring the actual required proof depth.
s63908ad4c4.why: Benchmarks and training data labeled by stated depth may misrepresent reasoning difficulty, affecting how models are evaluated and trained.

s2e47ed7ddb.title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis in Jacobian-Space: Language and Vision Models Agree Approximately Up to a Rotation
s2e47ed7ddb.description: arXiv:2611.33304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) posits that AI models converge toward a shared representation of the world, even when trained on different data modalities. Previous work has found evidence for the PRH in the activations of vision and language models. In this work, we ask whether vision and language models also converge in how they act on these representations: precisely, in how these internal representations affect the models' output. At a chosen layer of a transformer, the Jacobian lens gives every word in the vocabulary (or class in an image classifier) a vector in the hidden state: the vector that most increases the model's tendency to generate that word, at that position or later, or to predict that class. s2e47ed7ddb.summary: An arXiv paper tests whether vision and language models converge in how their internal representations affect outputs, using Jacobian-space analysis.

sefa382521a.title: Brand Recall and Category Accuracy in Language Models: An Audit of 1,000 B2B SaaS Brands
sefa382521a.description: arXiv:2611.33322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A language model can name a brand without classifying it correctly. This study measures these outcomes separately for 1,000 B2B SaaS brands across 333 product categories. On Gemma 4 12B, with no external retrieval, category prompts elicit 510 brands (51.0%). A separate five-candidate category probe ranks the reference label first for 787 brands, a distractor first for 194, and yields little separation for 19. Among the 981 separated rankings, the error rate is 19.8%. It falls to 3.5% for the 547 brands with a winner-to-runner-up log-probability margin above 0.6. sefa382521a.summary: An arXiv study finds Gemma 4 12B names many B2B SaaS brands without classifying them correctly, with separate measures of brand recall and category accuracy across 1,000 brands.
sefa382521a.why: Teams relying on LLMs for brand or market information should measure recall and classification errors separately, since a model can name a brand yet misclassify it.

saa03895220.title: Confidence scores for gated automation of large language models
saa03895220.description: arXiv:2611.33394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong capabilities in automated decision-making. However, LLMs may produce incorrect answers with high confidence, limiting their applicability in decisions that affect individuals and organizations. Reliable confidence scores are necessary to gate such decisions, and existing estimates are frequently unavailable or too coarse to support effective gating. This work uses supervised learning to train models to predict the correctness of LLM-generated answers, enabling automated confident responses and routing uncertain ones for human review. saa03895220.summary: An arXiv paper uses supervised learning to predict the correctness of LLM-generated answers, producing confidence scores to gate automated decisions.
saa03895220.why: Reliable per-answer confidence scores could let teams automate low-risk LLM decisions while routing uncertain ones to humans.

s6109b6ac57.title: Partial Routing: Trace-Tuned Delegation for Resource-Efficient Agentic Workflows
s6109b6ac57.description: arXiv:2611.33402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI models vary enormously in capability and price. Model routing exploits this by sending easier tasks to cheaper models. However, a single agentic task often combines easy and difficult subtasks, making one model choice for the entire task inefficient. We introduce partial routing, which guides a frontier lead model to delegate suitable subtasks to a cheaper worker model. From both models' past runs, we identify recurring subtasks and measure each model's quality and cost on them. s6109b6ac57.summary: An arXiv paper introduces partial routing, where a frontier model delegates suitable subtasks in agentic workflows to a cheaper worker model using trace-derived guidance.
s6109b6ac57.why: Delegating subtasks rather than whole tasks may reduce agent costs while keeping quality, which matters for production agent budgets.

s4cf7f9ebfa.title: Collaborative Language Models for Semantic IoT Data Processing: Validation through Zero-Shot Human Activity Recognition
s4cf7f9ebfa.description: arXiv:2611.33411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) systems generate low-level sensor observations that are not directly suitable for process analysis and must first be transformed into semantically meaningful events. This paper investigates collaborative language models as a zero-shot semantic abstraction layer for converting such observations into higher-level event and activity labels. We propose a five-stage workflow comprising semantic mapping, semantic aggregation, temporal and contextual aggregation, specialized reasoning, and final event abstraction. s4cf7f9ebfa.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a five-stage workflow using collaborative language models to turn raw IoT sensor data into semantic activity labels with zero-shot human activity recognition.
s4cf7f9ebfa.why: It offers a way to convert noisy sensor streams into event labels without task-specific training data.

s4dddd10969.title: Dynamic Reasoning in Next-Gen Detection and Response: An Empirical Study of LLM Triage, Reinforcement Tuning, and Adversarial Evasion
s4dddd10969.description: arXiv:2611.33470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an end-to-end empirical study of dynamic reasoning in next-generation detection and response pipelines, evaluating how static classifiers, graph-based signal fusion, and large language model (LLM) triage agents perform under strict human-analyst attention budgets (Recall at B alerts/day). s4dddd10969.why: Security teams get evidence on how LLM triage agents perform against analyst attention limits and adversarial evasion, though the results are from simulations and public datasets.

s80f404d8b5.title: CA-RAG: Constraint-Aligned Retrieval for Structurally Faithful Long-Form Generation
s80f404d8b5.description: arXiv:2611.33497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) typically optimises evidence selection for semantic relevance, whereas compliance-sensitive long-form generation also requires evidence supporting explicit structural obligations. Semantically relevant retrieval may therefore omit information needed for mandatory downstream clauses. s80f404d8b5.summary: An arXiv paper proposes CA-RAG, a retrieval method that adds ontology-derived structural constraints to queries so long-form generation includes evidence for mandatory clauses.
s80f404d8b5.why: Compliance-sensitive document generation may omit required clauses when retrieval optimizes only for semantic relevance, and this targets that gap.

s7e922b4c2c.title: Learning to Reason in Real-Time
s7e922b4c2c.description: arXiv:2611.33513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents that operate in the real world must reason correctly and on-time, yet they currently do not account for how time should alter their reasoning. Modern agents learn to do tasks in environments that are entirely synchronous: where the world waits for the agent to act before changing. A real-time environment, by contrast, changes independent of the agent. Existing approaches try to bridge this gap by imposing a ratio of thinking to acting. However, for an agent to succeed in real-time it must learn to act quickly when delay is costly and to reason longer when the benefit outweighs the missed opportunities. To this end, we introduce real-time reasoning training (RRT) as the class of training techniques for real-time reasoning agents. We
s7e922b4c2c.summary: An arXiv paper argues AI agents in real-time environments must learn to balance reasoning and action speed, since the world changes independently of the agent.
s7e922b4c2c.why: Agents acting in live environments face costs from delay that synchronous training setups do not capture, so timing-aware reasoning matters for deployment.

sbdb12eac8f.title: PeerReveal: Learning to Generalize in AI Peer Review Detection
sbdb12eac8f.description: arXiv:2611.33555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can we distinguish fully AI-generated reviews from those using AI only to rewrite human judgement? sbdb12eac8f.summary: Researchers introduce PeerReveal, a detector that distinguishes fully AI-generated peer reviews from human reviews merely rewritten with AI, tested on a new 5,430-review set.
sbdb12eac8f.why: Reliable detection of AI-written reviews matters to conference organizers and research teams building trust and integrity checks into review workflows.

sd132989012.title: FIG-MAC: A Fine-grained Inspiration Graph Empowered Multi-Agent Collaboration for Automated Scientific Hypothesis Generation
sd132989012.description: arXiv:2611.33563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated Scientific Hypothesis Generation (ASHG) leveraging large language models (LLMs) aims to harness their strengths in knowledge integration, logical reasoning, and text generation for efficiently producing innovative, verifiable scientific hypotheses. sd132989012.summary: FIG-MAC proposes a multi-agent framework using fine-grained inspiration graphs to improve LLM-based automated generation of scientific hypotheses.

s758ccd72bc.title: Aligned Machine: A Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Embedding Similarity via Human Comparative Judgements
s758ccd72bc.description: arXiv:2611.33594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Embedding models increasingly inform how people search, recommend, and retrieve information, yet we lack credible ways to test whether these similarity judgments reflect how humans understand meaning. s8c28a80eb4.title: Learning from Natural Images Untangles Number Sense
s8c28a80eb4.description: arXiv:2611.33615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Numerical cognition is a simple yet fundamental ability that remains challenging for modern vision-language models. Meanwhile, number sense is already present in numerically na\"ive animals, suggesting that it can emerge without explicit numerical learning. s0ec3cbaa6a.title: Controllable CAD Generation and Interactive Editing of Fluid Rotors
s0ec3cbaa6a.description: arXiv:2611.33617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computer-aided design (CAD) provides the geometric foundation for rotors in fluid rotating machinery. saf04c85c97.summary: Merlin-Bench is introduced to evaluate LLM agents' ability to produce verifiable proofs, drawing on interactive proof systems from complexity theory.
saf04c85c97.why: Evaluating whether agent outputs can be independently checked addresses a core reliability problem for LLMs in formal verification workflows.

s3d3bc7f2d8.title: Faster and Better Query (FBQ): Learning Future-Position Probes from the First Generated Token
s3d3bc7f2d8.description: arXiv:2611.33679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a large language model (LLM) evicts prompt keys and values at the end of prefill, it must decide what to keep before it sees the queries from subsequent decoding steps. Generating a draft continuation can approximate those queries at the cost of extra autoregressive steps. Can we use the embedding of the first output token, already available from the final prefill logits, to construct low-cost pseudo queries that approximate future decoding queries? s3d3bc7f2d8.summary: FBQ proposes using the first generated token's embedding to build low-cost pseudo queries for deciding which LLM prompt KV cache entries to keep during decoding.
s3d3bc7f2d8.why: Offers a way to improve KV cache eviction without extra draft decoding steps, relevant to teams optimizing LLM inference memory and latency.

s3fb02af113.title: EVA: Evidence-seeking Visual Agent for Hallucination-Resistant Multimodal Reasoning
s3fb02af113.description: arXiv:2611.33706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hallucinations in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often arise from visual assumptions that go unchecked. Self-reflection, multi-agent debate, and counterfactual verification can reinforce erroneous conclusions when they rely on the same unverified visual assumptions. External visual tools can provide verifiable evidence, but models may select the wrong tools, supply incorrect parameters, or ignore or contradict the evidence they obtain. s3fb02af113.summary: EVA is an evidence-seeking visual agent that uses external visual tools to verify assumptions and reduce hallucinations in multimodal LLM reasoning.
s3fb02af113.why: Grounding multimodal answers in verifiable tool evidence targets a practical hallucination problem for teams deploying vision-language systems.

sf0c5f52e5d.title: P-FedSkill: A Personalized Federated Skill Learning Framework under Task Heterogeneity
sf0c5f52e5d.description: arXiv:2611.33707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Skill learning has become an important way to improve agent performance. However, agent trajectories often contain sensitive information and cannot be shared across clients, hindering collaborative skill learning. To tackle this issue, federated skill learning (FSL) has emerged as a solution by distilling trajectories into compact skill representations and uploading them to a central server for sharing. However, existing FSL methods typically share skills based on skill similarity without considering their contributions to heterogeneous tasks across clients, thereby degrading agent performance. To address this challenge, we propose P-FedSkill, a personalized FSL framework that comprises three key components: local skill extraction (LSE), pers
sf0c5f52e5d.summary: P-FedSkill proposes a personalized federated skill learning framework that shares agent skills across clients with heterogeneous tasks without exposing sensitive trajectories.
sf0c5f52e5d.why: Addresses sharing learned agent skills across organizations without leaking sensitive trajectory data, a privacy concern for enterprise agent deployments.

s10f075af16.title: PowerFix: Physics-Guided Iterative Repair for LLM-Assisted Power Converter Design
s10f075af16.description: arXiv:2611.33712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly being explored for automated engineering design. However, repairing power-converter designs that fail engineering validation remains challenging: the system must identify physical causes, locate responsible design variables, and resolve violations without compromising other constraints. We introduce PowerFix, a physics-guided iterative repair framework that converts validation failures into structured diagnoses and executable patches while preserving topology and design requirements. PowerDiagGraph links failed checks to possible physical causes and constrains repair routes. An LLM prioritizes these routes, while a deterministic compiler translates selected repairs into authorized field-level
s10f075af16.summary: PowerFix is a physics-guided iterative repair framework that turns validation failures into structured diagnoses and patches for LLM-generated power converter designs.
s10f075af16.why: Shows a method for LLM design agents to repair failing engineering designs while preserving constraints, relevant to automated hardware design teams.

s7c12f552f9.title: KeyDeck: Multi-Paper-to-Slide Generation via Cross-Paper Synthesis and Reference-Guided Personalization
s7c12f552f9.description: arXiv:2611.33715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-paper-to-slide generation (multi-PTSG) is the task of constructing a unified presentation from multiple research papers by selecting, organizing, and synthesizing information across sources. This task introduces two main challenges: (i) combining multiple sources into a coherent narrative requires identifying cross-paper relationships and synthesizing their content, and (ii) the desired organization and emphasis varies substantially across presenters, making personalization essential for user satisfaction. Motivated by these challenges, we propose KeyDeck, the first multi-PTSG framework that integrates per-paper and cross-paper analysis to identify relationships among sources and synthesize their contributions into a coherent narrative,
s7c12f552f9.summary: KeyDeck introduces multi-paper-to-slide generation that synthesizes cross-paper content and personalizes presentations to presenter preferences.

sd0e11bb3c2.title: Asset4D-Bench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Editable 3D and 4D Reconstruction
sd0e11bb3c2.description: arXiv:2611.33728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A cart can follow its reference trajectory while its cargo floats above the deck. Asset4D-Bench tests whether coding agents recover objects, motion and interactions from visual references as editable Blender scenes. Its 114 conditions span image editing, video reconstruction with matched full or partial starter assets, and independently selected from-scratch tasks. We independently reopen projects and measure them against native reference states. The 228 archived scores include original delivery outcomes and versioned measures of scene quality. On 24 from-scratch tasks, each model earns full dynamics credit on 14. Of these, three GPT-6.1-Sol and eight GPT-6-Astra reconstructions earn zero relation points. sd0e11bb3c2.summary: Asset4D-Bench benchmarks coding agents on recovering editable 3D and 4D Blender scenes from visual references across 114 conditions.
sd0e11bb3c2.why: Provides a benchmark for evaluating coding agents on 3D content creation tasks, useful for teams building agentic creative or simulation tooling.

sbd0e3791a2.title: JOVE ICE: Intent Guided Cloud Edge Device Collaboration for AI Glasses
sbd0e3791a2.description: arXiv:2611.33735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and LLM based agents have expanded the capabilities of AI glasses, enabling egocentric visual question answering, memory retrieval, and proactive assistance. These applications involve diverse inputs, including speech, images, and video, and range from simple device control to complex visual reasoning, posing challenges for efficient computation and communication. While video centric capabilities have received considerable attention, simple text based and device executable tasks remain underexplored despite their prevalence in daily interactions. Efficiently supporting diverse workloads within a unified assistant remains an open challenge. We propose JOVE ICE, an intent guided cloud, edge, and d
sbd0e3791a2.summary: JOVE ICE proposes intent-guided collaboration between cloud and device for AI glasses, routing simple text and device-executable tasks differently from video workloads.
sbd0e3791a2.why: Intent-based splitting of work between edge and cloud is a useful pattern for latency and cost tradeoffs in on-device AI products.

s035874d82c.title: WhatIf: Counterfactual World Models over Action-Grounded Causal Graphs for Robotic Manipulation
s035874d82c.description: arXiv:2611.33745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World models predict what happens under an action, but choosing between actions requires comparing their outcomes in the same physical situation. Factual transitions alone determine action-wise marginal futures and average effects, but not individual effects or the probability that switching actions causes harm. We introduce WhatIf, a counterfactual world model for manipulation that couples candidate futures through shared latent physics and transition noise inferred from factual history. s035874d82c.summary: Researchers propose WhatIf, a counterfactual world model for robotic manipulation that compares candidate action outcomes under shared latent physics inferred from factual history.
s035874d82c.why: It addresses comparing actions in the same physical situation, which matters for robot planning and evaluating harm from switching actions.

sf3bdc8f3bc.title: REFORGE: LLM-Assisted RTL Bug Repair with Structured Context and Verification Feedback
sf3bdc8f3bc.description: arXiv:2611.33748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can write and repair RTL, but successful compilation or testbench execution does not establish defect removal, behavioral preservation, security, or implementation feasibility. Existing LLM-based RTL repair methods often report a single repair rate without retaining separate evidence for these properties, limiting reproducible comparison and integration into hardware design flows. We present REFORGE, which, to our knowledge, is the first LLM-assisted RTL repair framework that maintains and accumulates structured repair evidence across iterations, allowing it to generate fixes that satisfy multiple objectives simultaneously, including functionality, behavioral equivalence, security, and cost efficiency. REFORGE pro
sf3bdc8f3bc.summary: Researchers present REFORGE, an LLM-assisted RTL bug repair framework that keeps separate evidence for defect removal, behavioral preservation, security, and feasibility.
sf3bdc8f3bc.why: Compilation or passing testbenches alone do not prove a hardware repair is correct, so separated evidence aids reproducible comparison and integration into design flows.

s5f6caed495.title: TransHarness: From Benchmark Overfitting to Transferable Harness Evolution
s5f6caed495.description: arXiv:2611.33757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Harness evolution offers a path to improving coding agents without updating model weights. However, existing methods can overfit their evolution benchmarks, producing gains that fail to carry over to new tasks. To address this challenge, we introduce Transferable Harness Evolution (TransHarness), which evolves harness intervention policies from same-task success-failure contrasts. These policies couple execution-context triggers with diagnostic guidance, enabling task-dependent checks and corrections beyond the source executions. Cross-task replay and independent semantic selection retain policies that intervene selectively and ground corrections in current-task evidence rather than source-specific solutions. We further curate an independent
s5f6caed495.summary: Researchers introduce TransHarness, a method that evolves coding-agent harness intervention policies from success-failure contrasts so gains transfer to new tasks instead of overfitting benchmarks.
s5f6caed495.why: It offers a way to improve coding agents without updating model weights, with gains that generalize beyond the evolution benchmark.

s313b762197.title: Improving Building Energy Efficiency with an Indoor Environmental World Model and Counterfactual Adaptive Learning
s313b762197.description: arXiv:2611.33764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimizing indoor climate systems plays a critical role in achieving the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals 11 and 13. However, indoor delayed thermodynamic responses and partial observability severely hinder existing reinforcement learning (RL) methods, which are primarily limited by implicit thermal inertia, occupancy dynamic prediction, and cumulative prediction errors during long-horizon rollouts. Thus, we propose a novel occupant-centric indoor climate control framework. It develops indoor environmental world models to predict future physical thermal baselines and dynamic occupancy, explicitly capturing latent thermal inertia. By formulating adaptive regulation as counterfactual advantage learning against future environments v
s313b762197.summary: Researchers propose an occupant-centric indoor climate control framework that uses indoor environmental world models and counterfactual adaptive learning to improve building energy efficiency.
s313b762197.why: It applies world-model-based reinforcement learning to building control, where thermal inertia and partial observability hinder existing methods.

s0a7b71b792.title: CHD-Bench: Diagnosing Congenital Heart Disease through Interactive Examination
s0a7b71b792.description: arXiv:2611.33775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diagnosis of congenital heart disease (CHD) requires understanding the spatial relationships between cardiac structures, which clinicians assess by scrolling through CT or cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) slices and rotating 3D reconstructions. Although automated methods have advanced cardiac segmentation, identifying congenital heart defects from volumetric scans remains an open challenge. The two existing approaches rely on handcrafted diagnostic rules limited to static anatomical abnormalities. We introduce CHD-Bench, the first benchmark for interactive CHD diagnosis, defining a multi-label task and evaluation protocol over 247 CT and MRI scans from three cohorts covering 38 CHD types. We also present CHD-Harness, open-source softw
s0a7b71b792.summary: Researchers introduce CHD-Bench, a benchmark for diagnosing congenital heart disease through interactive examination of CT and MRI volumes rather than static anatomical rules.

sf15ab42622.title: InterGenEHR$^+$: An Interactive Framework for Natural Language-Conditioned Generation of Longitudinal Patient Trajectories
sf15ab42622.description: arXiv:2611.33788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Objective: To develop and validate InterGenEHR$^+$, an interactive framework for natural language-conditioned generation of synthetic tabular electronic health records (EHRs) and longitudinal trajectories for scenario-based evaluation of machine learning models. Methods: An optional large language model (LLM) parser converts clinical requests into structured constraints. Conditional variational autoencoders and diffusion models generate single-time-point records, while diffusion models generate longitudinal trajectories. sf15ab42622.summary: Researchers present InterGenEHR+, an interactive framework that generates synthetic tabular and longitudinal EHR data from natural language requests using an optional LLM parser and diffusion models.
sf15ab42622.why: Synthetic patient data generated from natural language scenarios could support scenario-based testing of clinical machine learning models.

s1fe898ecb2.title: ExtractBench Pro: The Long Tail of Document Extraction
s1fe898ecb2.description: arXiv:2611.33791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present ExtractBench Pro, a schema-guided document extraction benchmark that tests six challenging modes of extraction underrepresented in existing datasets. It is created following a framework for synthetic document generation, in which deterministic document generators assemble challenging components into documents that are designed to be difficult at a level calibrated for frontier systems. We synthesize 100 realistic documents spanning a diverse range of styles. On this data, we evaluate ten coding agents and eight extraction API configurations for accuracy, grounding, and their ability to perfectly extract documents. s1fe898ecb2.summary: Researchers released ExtractBench Pro, a schema-guided document extraction benchmark of 100 synthetic documents, and evaluated ten coding agents and eight extraction API configurations on it.
s1fe898ecb2.why: It offers a harder test of extraction tools on long-tail document cases, helping teams compare coding agents and extraction APIs.

s06d40dbaf8.title: Keep or Roll Back? Out-of-Loop Judges for Self-Improving VLA and End-to-End Embodied Policies
s06d40dbaf8.description: arXiv:2611.33794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-improvement is now a practical recipe for embodied policies: a policy collects experience, is retrained, and is kept when a judge rates it higher. However, the judge is usually trained or chosen inside the same loop, so its evidence is not independent of the policy. We introduce SealedLoop, an evaluation framework that adds a sealed judge: an evaluator outside the loop that the improver cannot see or optimize against. A new policy is kept only when a sequential test on the sealed judge confirms the gain, with a bounded probability of keeping a worse one. s06d40dbaf8.summary: Researchers introduce SealedLoop, an evaluation framework that uses a judge outside the training loop to decide whether self-improved embodied policies should be kept.
s06d40dbaf8.why: Self-improvement loops often judge with evidence not independent of the policy; a sealed evaluator can guard against false gains before deployment.

sac3e37b3c3.title: Ensuring Deployment-Time Safety of Neural Network Controlled Systems via Localized Certificate Repair
sac3e37b3c3.description: arXiv:2611.33813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Barrier certificates provide formal safety guarantees for neural network controlled systems by ensuring that system trajectories avoid unsafe regions over time. However, after deployment, previously unseen obstacles or constraint changes may introduce new unsafe regions, invalidating the original certificate and potentially leading to unsafe behavior. sac3e37b3c3.summary: Researchers propose adaptive piecewise barrier certificates that locally repair safety certificates for neural network controlled systems when new unsafe regions appear after deployment.
sac3e37b3c3.why: Deployed controllers facing new obstacles or constraint changes can be updated locally while preserving the original certificate in unchanged regions.

s33738813d8.title: Spectral Optimal Transport for Dynamics-Aware Sign Language Generation
s33738813d8.description: arXiv:2611.33818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sign language generation (SLG) translates spoken-language text into pose sequences that convey its meaning. Recently, flow-based models with optimal transport (OT) have become a strong SLG baseline by handling the one-to-many nature of text-to-sign. While classifier-free guidance (CFG) could be applied to further strengthen the semantic alignment theoretically, its training involves conditional and unconditional training, which may contradict the pose-space OT, thus reducing the generation quality. s33738813d8.summary: Researchers propose a spectral optimal transport approach for dynamics-aware sign language generation that aims to improve classifier-free guidance in flow-based pose generation.

s271dd9ffff.title: RadOncGym: An Agent-Based Framework for Radiotherapy Dose-Mimicking Optimization
s271dd9ffff.description: arXiv:2611.33821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI dose-prediction models generate patient-specific 3D dose distributions from patient anatomy, providing an important intermediate representation for automated radiotherapy planning. However, an AI-predicted dose must undergo downstream optimization to produce a physically constrained treatment plan, a process that requires balancing competing planning objectives. We present RadOncGym, an agent-based framework that enables an LLM agent to iteratively tune 12 planning-objective weights for dose-mimicking optimization. s271dd9ffff.summary: Researchers present RadOncGym, an agent-based framework where an LLM iteratively tunes 12 planning-objective weights for dose-mimicking radiotherapy plan optimization.
s271dd9ffff.why: It shows an LLM agent tuning optimization parameters in a regulated medical planning loop, though the text gives limited detail on outcomes.

s551923581e.title: MetaDecomp: Adaptive Task Decomposition via Meta-Learned Procedural Memory
s551923581e.description: arXiv:2611.33822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reusing past experience in long-horizon tasks requires more than storing successful procedures: Language agents must distinguish which procedures apply and what work remains as execution progresses. We introduce MetaDecomp, an in-context meta-learning framework for adaptive task decomposition that jointly learns a task-relative state space and reusable procedures. s551923581e.summary: Researchers introduce MetaDecomp, an in-context meta-learning framework that builds procedural memory from successful executions to adaptively decompose long-horizon tasks for language agents.
s551923581e.why: Reusable procedures stored as state graphs could help agents pick applicable strategies and track remaining work on long tasks.

s6629749d0b.title: Can Its Own Misses Teach an MLLM to Find Small Brain Metastases?
s6629749d0b.description: arXiv:2611.33836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are becoming general readers of medical images, yet they remain weak at locating small abnormalities. Brain metastases expose this gap: at 384 px a 0.1 mL lesion covers less than a quarter of one visual token, and at one false positive per scan frontier MLLMs find fewer than 30% of lesions of 0.1-1 mL. Fine-tuning on one dataset helps but transfers poorly, and improving it further is slow trial and error steered by a single score. s6629749d0b.summary: Researchers introduce LANTERN, an error-driven recursive method that helps multimodal LLMs find small brain metastases, which frontier models currently miss often on 0.1-1 mL lesions.
s6629749d0b.why: It targets a clear weakness of MLLMs in medical imaging, where small lesions are hard to locate and fine-tuning transfers poorly.

s65d99987a2.title: FORK: Co-Evolving Safe Disclosure and Decision Skills Against Attackers Who Read Every Refusal
s65d99987a2.description: arXiv:2611.33879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a guardrail rejects an LLM agent's action, its message reaches any attacker observing the trajectory: a fixed refusal leaves benign users unable to recover, whereas an explanation can tell the attacker what to try next. s65d99987a2.summary: Researchers study safe disclosure, explaining LLM agent guardrail refusals so benign users recover without helping attackers, and co-evolve disclosure and decision skills.
s65d99987a2.why: Refusal messages can leak information to attackers, so guardrail designers must balance explanation quality against adaptive attack success.

s30c37cc37f.title: EATS: Scaling Tool-Use Experience for Medical Reasoning Agents
s30c37cc37f.description: arXiv:2611.33897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medical reasoning agents combine large language model (LLM) reasoning with clinical workflows and specialized neural tools. However, general-purpose LLMs receive limited training exposure to domain-specific medical tools, and the uncertainty and distributional shifts of neural tool outputs make selecting tools from simple descriptions significantly more challenging than in deterministic settings such as calculators or dictionary lookups. In this paper, we propose EATS, an experience-augmented tool selection strategy that leverages accumulated tool-use trajectories to improve tool selection in medical reasoning agents. s30c37cc37f.summary: Researchers propose EATS, an experience-augmented tool selection strategy that uses accumulated tool-use experience to help medical reasoning agents choose neural clinical tools.
s30c37cc37f.why: Selecting among uncertain neural tool outputs is harder than with deterministic tools, and experience-based selection targets that gap for agent builders.

s3e0aa1bb01.title: EGSE: Evidence-Grounded Skill Evolution for Medical Reasoning Agents
s3e0aa1bb01.description: arXiv:2611.33909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medical reasoning agents combine foundation models with specialized tools to interpret medical images, yet reusing their historical experience remains challenging. A correct final answer can conceal flawed reasoning or tool use, synthesized advice may lack source support, and superficially similar cases may require different diagnostic procedures. s3e0aa1bb01.summary: EGSE is a framework that distills historical dialogues from similar medical cases into reusable conditional workflows for medical reasoning agents that interpret images.
s3e0aa1bb01.why: Shows a way to reuse agent experience while checking that correct answers reflect sound reasoning and tool use, not luck.

sf6df3ac7e3.title: What Does Skill Lift Actually Measure? A Source-Code-Level Audit and Noise-Aware Reanalysis of SkillsBench
sf6df3ac7e3.description: arXiv:2611.33943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills are directories of instructions, reference materials, and scripts loaded on demand by coding agents. According to SkillsBench, although human-curated skills can raise the passing rate by about 16.6 percentage points (pp) on average, they have actually reduced the results for some tasks. Later research has started to gate or eliminate skills according to the above per-task gains. We have audited the above benchmark at the source-code level and analysed 7,554 public trials to form 1,421 paired "(configuration, task) cells". sf6df3ac7e3.why: Challenges benchmark-based claims that agent skills improve pass rates, so teams should check evaluation methods before relying on skill gains.

s8ff3be331d.title: Should Service Requirements Be Scalarized or Constrained When Minimizing Costs? A Case Study on HVAC Control
s8ff3be331d.description: arXiv:2611.33946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated decision systems, from learned policies to model-based optimizers, often minimize costs such as energy or resource use while meeting a service requirement, for example the quality of service (QoS) specified in a service level agreement (SLA), a comfort band, or a safety margin. s8ff3be331d.summary: A case study on HVAC control in the Smart Buildings Challenge compares scalarizing service requirements into the cost objective versus imposing them as constraints.
s8ff3be331d.why: Helps engineers choose how to encode SLA or comfort requirements in cost-minimizing automated control systems.

s1c2746193c.title: PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models
s1c2746193c.description: arXiv:2611.33966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There are several approaches to AI-driven mathematical discovery. One of these involves the use of large language models (LLMs) to resolve well-specified conjectures via text-based reasoning, while another uses narrow models and interpretability for more open-ended, human-in-the-loop exploration using object-based mathematical data. The latter is limited in its ability to move beyond simple empirical pattern detection while the former is not well-designed for direct, open-ended exploration of large mathematical datasets. s1c2746193c.summary: PatternMiner is a framework that uses LLM guidance to train and interpret small models for open-ended mathematical discovery on large datasets.

sa236997ea8.title: Honest but Wrong: Formalizing Retraction in the Ethics of Speech Acts
sa236997ea8.description: arXiv:2611.34011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A speaker who asserts honestly may later discover that its assertion was false. Such erroneous truths are not lies, yet they raise the question of whether, and on which moral grounds, the speaker must retract them. sa236997ea8.summary: A paper formalizes retraction of honestly made but false assertions within a belief-based speech-act framework, proving deontologism's honesty duty never requires retracting them.

sed7660ba87.title: Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models via Agentic Model Editing
sed7660ba87.description: arXiv:2611.34036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Few-shot adaptation transfers pretrained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to new domains using a small set of labeled images. Most methods fit prompts, representations, or classifiers within an adaptation procedure specified in advance. sed7660ba87.summary: Agentic Model Editing (AME) proposes an LLM agent that designs the few-shot adaptation procedure for vision-language models, including input transforms, from few labeled images.
sed7660ba87.why: Suggests agents could automate adaptation design for VLMs rather than relying on fixed prompt or classifier pipelines.

s9d9674ee2d.title: Budget, Readout or Reasoning? Where Small Reasoning Models Lose Value in Auction Bidding
s9d9674ee2d.description: arXiv:2611.34068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ad platforms and marketplaces show bidders a bid landscape, the estimated chance of winning at each candidate bid, and increasingly let agents built on reasoning language models choose the bid. s9d9674ee2d.summary: Researchers evaluated six open reasoning models of 4B to 14B parameters on auction bidding, splitting lost value into causes such as budget, readout, and reasoning failures.
s9d9674ee2d.why: Indicates where small reasoning models fail in bidding agents, informing whether to fix estimates, decision logic, or model capacity.

sda43a02054.title: Not Every Input Needs Everything: Unifying Expert Gating, Model Cascades, and Agent Orchestration
sda43a02054.description: arXiv:2611.34112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Executing monolithic neural weights, frontier foundation models, or entire multi-agent workflows uniformly on every input incurs substantial computational, latency, and monetary overhead. Conditional computation mitigates this cost by deciding dynamically which internal experts, model endpoints, or specialized agents to invoke per request. Yet token-level gating in sparse neural architectures, query-level model cascades, and task-level multi-agent coordination have largely progressed in disconnected research silos, obscuring recurring system failures and transferable fixes. sda43a02054.summary: A paper unifies expert gating, model cascades, and multi-agent orchestration as conditional computation approaches that decide which experts, models, or agents to invoke per request.
sda43a02054.why: Offers a common framing for cutting compute, latency, and cost by routing requests to only the components each input needs.

s5ddc80c89f.title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand
s5ddc80c89f.description: arXiv:2611.34147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent harnesses today manage context on the model's behalf: when the window fills, the harness triggers a compaction that summarizes the history. We study the alternative, \emph{model-driven} context management, in which the model itself decides when and what to compact through a context API. We gave models control over their own context in \nooa, NVIDIA's open source agent harness, and compared the two strategies on document research and machine learning engineering across context budgets from 8K to 512K tokens. s5ddc80c89f.summary: NVIDIA researchers compared model-driven context management, where models decide when and what to compact via a context API, against harness-triggered compaction in its open source agent harness.
s5ddc80c89f.why: Gives engineers evidence on whether letting models manage their own context beats automatic summarization across budgets from 8K to 512K tokens.

s37d15bd370.title: SOLO: Towards Sample-Faithful and Detectable LLM Watermarking under Repeated Sampling via Content-Anchored Single-Owner Contexts
s37d15bd370.description: arXiv:2611.34190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Providers watermark the outputs of large language models, while applications sample many responses per prompt for self-consistency, best-of-n selection, and uncertainty estimation. s37d15bd370.why: Shows deployed distortion-free watermarks can collide across repeated samples, affecting detection for apps using self-consistency or best-of-n.

s2b73c37364.title: PROVE: Mitigating Long-Horizon LLM Collusion with Reinforcement Learning from Verified Evidence
s2b73c37364.description: arXiv:2611.34215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When LLM agents verify each other's work over a long interaction, they drift into collusion: they come to accept work without the evidence that the verification protocol requires. Collusion is absent at the start and builds up episode by episode, which we trace to accurate feedback accumulating in memory. An agent that follows the rule is told that its verdict was wrong whenever its peer was right, so breaking the rule is the reward-maximizing choice, and agents talk themselves into it in their private reflections. Existing mitigations leave the agents unchanged; we train the behavior out. s2b73c37364.summary: PROVE uses reinforcement learning from verified evidence to reduce long-horizon collusion among LLM agents that verify each other's work without required evidence.
s2b73c37364.why: Highlights that multi-agent verification pipelines can drift into accepting unsupported work, a reliability risk for agent systems.

s3dc5666ad1.title: Did the Model Forecast It, or Already Know It? Evaluating Large Language Models for Novel Drug-Target Prioritisation with a Temporal Knowledge-Graph Oracle
s3dc5666ad1.description: arXiv:2611.34247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems increasingly help decide which drug targets enter costly clinical trials. We recast each target-disease hypothesis as a dated event, the pair's first clinical trial. This lets us test whether a language model can forecast such events after its training cutoff, rather than recall events before it. We rebuild a dated biomedical knowledge graph as it stood at the end of each year from 2020 up to its newest version. We then ask six open language models, with and without this graph, which targets will enter a first trial for a disease the next year. s3dc5666ad1.summary: Researchers rebuilt a dated biomedical knowledge graph and tested six open language models on forecasting which drug targets will enter a first clinical trial after training cutoffs.
s3dc5666ad1.why: Separates genuine forecasting from recall of past events, relevant to teams evaluating AI for drug-target prioritisation.

s4dae22ce7d.title: EXPOSURE: Explaining Sources of Uncertainty in Reinforcement Learning
s4dae22ce7d.description: arXiv:2611.34248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shapley values in reinforcement learning are used to explain which observation features drive an agent's behavior and expected return, but not its certainty. Explaining certainty requires understanding how observation features influence different sources of return uncertainty, and Shapley values need the agent's prediction for every subset of visible features. We propose EXPOSURE, which uses one mask-aware belief network for both action selection and Shapley explanations. s4dae22ce7d.summary: EXPOSURE uses a mask-aware belief network to explain sources of return variance in reinforcement learning agents, splitting uncertainty into observational and other parts.

s2806cd06eb.title: Navigent: A Geometry-Grounded Agentic Framework for Vision Language Navigation
s2806cd06eb.description: arXiv:2611.34249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) with general-purpose multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offers a flexible alternative to task-specific navigation policies, while reliable long-horizon execution remains challenging. Agents must track navigation progress, detect discrepancies between commanded and actual motion, and recognize when movement has passed relevant landmarks or entrances. We present Navigent, an agentic VLN framework built around a frozen MLLM and a Geometry-Grounded Execution Critic (GEC). s2806cd06eb.summary: Navigent is an agentic vision-language navigation framework built on a frozen multimodal LLM and a Geometry-Grounded Execution Critic that checks progress and motion discrepancies.
s2806cd06eb.why: Shows how adding a geometric execution critic can improve reliability of long-horizon MLLM-driven agents without retraining the base model.

sd60456d644.title: MedSkill-E$^{2}$: Evaluating and Evolving Skills for Medical Agents
sd60456d644.description: arXiv:2611.34250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly use skills to access domain knowledge and complete real-world tasks. We observe that even when a skill specifies the rules and procedures needed for a task, agents may fail to apply them effectively during autonomous execution, a phenomenon we call skill Enable But Underuse (EBU). This issue is particularly consequential in medical tasks, where overlooking a single critical constraint can yield a plausible but incorrect result. sd60456d644.summary: MedSkill-E2 is a framework to evaluate and evolve skills for medical LLM agents, targeting cases where agents fail to apply skill rules they were given, called Enable But Underuse.
sd60456d644.why: Points to a failure mode where agents ignore provided constraints, which matters for any agent relying on skills in high-stakes domains.

sf4359170ef.title: Crucible: Evaluating LLM Agents in Executable Chemistry Research Environments
sf4359170ef.description: arXiv:2611.34254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform well on chemistry knowledge benchmarks, which mainly assess question answering and isolated tasks. Chemical research, however, requires using specialized tools and interpreting their outputs to obtain chemically valid results. To address this gap, we introduce Crucible Bench to evaluate this ability across all four stages of the design-make-test-analyze (DMTA) cycle. The benchmark contains 1,078 tasks in 12 task families curated from 18 published datasets, covering molecular design, synthesis planning, experimental execution, closed-loop optimization, simulation, and analytical characterization. sf4359170ef.summary: Researchers introduced Crucible Bench, a 1,078-task benchmark testing LLM agents on specialized chemistry tools across the design-make-test-analyze cycle.
sf4359170ef.why: It shows where LLM agents fall short on executable, tool-driven scientific workflows beyond chemistry Q&A, useful for evaluating domain agents.

s0904d61097.title: MeterRouter: Budget-Aware Dynamic Routing for Multi-Agent Systems
s0904d61097.description: arXiv:2611.34327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs) outperform single-agent systems, but inter-agent communication incurs substantial token overhead. While assigning a large LLM to every agent is common, it results in inefficient resource utilization, leaving the system far from the Pareto frontier. The cost of answering a query is set jointly by how many agents are recruited, the role and LLM assigned to each, and communication topology among them. s0904d61097.summary: MeterRouter proposes a budget-aware router that explicitly optimizes cost when choosing how many agents, which LLMs, and which communication topology to use in multi-agent systems.
s0904d61097.why: Multi-agent systems incur heavy token overhead, so explicit cost-aware routing could cut inference spend without sacrificing quality.

s7e489d2c94.title: EvoLink-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Interdependent Task Streams
s7e489d2c94.description: arXiv:2611.34400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are evolving from passive chatbots into autonomous systems that operate continuously in dynamic environments. Such agents need not only solve current tasks but also learn from past interactions to improve future performance. However, existing streaming benchmarks often rely on short task sequences or largely independent tasks, providing limited evidence of whether agents can effectively reuse experience when later tasks depend on earlier outcomes. s7e489d2c94.summary: EvoLink-Bench is a benchmark testing self-evolving LLM agents on long task streams where later tasks depend on earlier outcomes, measuring experience reuse.
s7e489d2c94.why: It targets whether agents truly learn from past interactions in dependent workflows, a gap that short or independent-task benchmarks miss.

sf64f41971a.title: Agentic Waterfall: An Intent-Driven Information Discovery Framework for Reclaiming User Control in the Attention Economy
sf64f41971a.description: arXiv:2611.34407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formalize Agentic Waterfall Feed, a new problem of personalized information discovery in which users actively direct recommendations and the system adapts to evolving needs inferred from both explicit requests and browsing behavior. We address this problem with the Agentic Waterfall framework, whose language-model controller maintains persistent user state and coordinates content retrieval, ranking, and state updates. sf64f41971a.summary: The Agentic Waterfall framework uses a language-model controller with persistent user state to let users direct personalized information discovery, along with a new dataset and replay-based evaluation.

s7d8787110a.title: Evaluating Aviation Safety Knowledge Extraction with SmolLM2: From Zero-Shot to Retrieval-Grounded Prompting
s7d8787110a.description: arXiv:2611.34432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aviation accident narratives contain safety knowledge that is difficult to capture using structured occurrence fields alone. This study evaluates prompting-based knowledge extraction across four dimensions: concept accuracy, verbatim evidence grounding, structural compliance, and directed relation extraction. SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct was evaluated under zero-shot, one-shot, fixed few-shot, and retrieval-grounded prompting using 300 National Transportation Safety Board narratives from 2000-2020, containing 3,763 reference concepts and 467 directed relations. s7d8787110a.summary: A study evaluates the small SmolLM2-1.7B model on extracting safety knowledge from 300 aviation accident narratives under zero-shot, few-shot, and retrieval-grounded prompting.
s7d8787110a.why: It offers evidence on how small open models perform on domain knowledge extraction under different prompting strategies, relevant to cost-constrained deployments.

sf712b8344c.title: vSFT: Learning to Verbally Tune Agents at Test Time
sf712b8344c.description: arXiv:2611.34440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly improved via agentic reinforcement learning, which can be on-policy but suffers from expensive rollouts and sparse rewards, limiting its application at test time. In this paper, we present a verbally Supervised Fine-Tuning (vSFT) framework that enables the conjunction of dense feedback in natural language and weight updates at test time. Specifically, our vSFT forms a closed loop between an agent and a supervisor via a hypernetwork, in which the supervisor generates verbal supervision from the agent's failed trajectories, and the hypernetwork converts that supervision into low-rank weight updates to tune the agent. sf712b8344c.summary: vSFT proposes a verbally supervised fine-tuning framework where a supervisor generates natural-language feedback and a hypernetwork updates agent weights at test time.
sf712b8344c.why: Combining dense natural-language feedback with test-time weight updates could reduce reliance on expensive on-policy rollouts and sparse rewards.

s653fb27d2e.title: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
s653fb27d2e.description: arXiv:2611.34466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI wearables, such as smart glasses, extend the context available to agents beyond digital environments to users' physical surroundings. With these devices, computer tasks can originate from users' ongoing activities rather than solely from explicit instructions. Through first-person observations, agents can identify objects and activities relevant to user requests and ground digital tasks in the surrounding context. We call this interaction paradigm Ego Use. s653fb27d2e.summary: EgoUseBench benchmarks computer-use agents that draw on first-person observations from AI wearables like smart glasses to ground digital tasks in users' surroundings.
s653fb27d2e.why: It highlights a new input modality for agents, where physical context from wearables drives computer tasks, which affects future agent design.

s42a679e9ef.title: On Utilization of Edge-AI for condition monitoring towards predictive maintenance: A use case in dairy processing using explainable AI
s42a679e9ef.description: arXiv:2611.34563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are driving Industry 4.0, enhancing productivity, automation, and efficiency in manufacturing systems. This study develops an Edge-AI-based condition monitoring framework, as a step towards predictive maintenance, for a rotary valve in a dairy processing pilot plant, using vibration data collected via a low-power IIoT sensor node and processed on an edge device.
s42a679e9ef.summary: Researchers developed an Edge-AI condition monitoring framework using vibration data and explainable AI to monitor a rotary valve in a dairy processing pilot plant.

s4e46bce9e7.title: Procedure Inference as Memory: Learning Recruiter Decision Procedures from OKF-Structured Episodes in Multi-Session Hiring Assistants
s4e46bce9e7.description: arXiv:2611.34576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-session hiring assistants must infer evolving recruiter preferences and decision patterns across projects and time. We introduce Open Knowledge Format (OKF)-indexed episodic memory to organize interactions and retrieve related events through their lineage. We also introduce Procedure Memory, which learns reusable decision procedures from these episodes through prompted reflection or reinforcement learning. s4e46bce9e7.why: Procedure memory that learns reusable decision patterns from interaction history offers a design pattern for long-running enterprise assistants.

s1128633fb0.title: Do We Really Need an LLM for Weight-Space Programming? A Deterministic Forward-Only Paradigm and Its Capability Boundaries
s1128633fb0.description: arXiv:2611.34612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work on Weight-Space Programming uses LLMs to edit neural weights with forward passes only, conflating LLM scripting with the underlying algebra of forward-only editing. s1128633fb0.why: If a deterministic pipeline matches LLM-driven weight editing in structured cases, it could lower cost and complexity for model editing workflows.

s2f31d0647a.title: HoMe: Toward Practical Harness Optimization of Memory Systems for AI Assistants
s2f31d0647a.description: arXiv:2611.34624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The behavior of memory systems for long-running AI assistants is governed by a harness, which consists of the code, prompts, and configurations for memory construction, maintenance, retrieval, and answer generation. s2f31d0647a.why: Automating harness optimization for memory systems could reduce manual tuning effort for assistants that need persistent context.

s8b1416f29c.title: ZeroHero: Training Small Language Agents from Scratch
s8b1416f29c.description: arXiv:2611.34635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large pretrained language models provide capable policies for interactive tasks, but how much model capacity is necessary for a specialized language agent? We introduce ZeroHero, a framework for training small language agents (SLAs) from scratch. In each environment, a large language model acts as the expert, and we collect its successful trajectories. We pretrain each SLA, which has fewer than 50 million parameters, to predict the expert's responses given the interaction history. s8b1416f29c.summary: ZeroHero trains small language agents with fewer than 50 million parameters from scratch, using expert LLM trajectories for pretraining and then self-interaction post-training.
s8b1416f29c.why: It suggests task-specific agents may not need large pretrained models, which could reduce serving costs for narrow environments.

sfa1af3715a.title: REE: A Scientific Research Entrance Exam for AI Agents
sfa1af3715a.description: arXiv:2611.34646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous research agents are emerging as a promising approach to scientific problem-solving across disciplines, owing to their growing ability to improve a solution through repeated experiments. Evaluating this ability requires benchmarks that pose open-ended research problems and measure improvements over established scientific methods. We introduce REE (Research Entrance Exam), a benchmark that tests AI agents on scientific research. sfa1af3715a.summary: REE is a benchmark of 100 open-ended research problems across five scientific areas and 23 domains, testing whether AI research agents improve solutions over established methods.
sfa1af3715a.why: It provides a harder, open-ended evaluation for research agents than fixed-answer benchmarks, useful for judging scientific automation claims.

sfcf1acf95d.title: A Failure-Driven Data Flywheel for Post-Training Vision-Language-Action Models
sfcf1acf95d.description: arXiv:2611.34698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) models rarely satisfy all behavioral requirements of a new platform, and teams without a large deployed fleet lack the data to address the resulting failures. We propose a failure-driven data flywheel for post-training such models. sfcf1acf95d.summary: A failure-driven data flywheel constructs missing target scenarios by inserting entities into reconstructed scenes to post-train vision-language-action robot models without a large fleet.
sfcf1acf95d.why: Teams without large deployed fleets can use synthetic failure-targeted data to improve robot policies, lowering the data barrier for VLA models.

s81a46184d9.title: From Shared Patterns to Individual Evidence: Two-Stage Reasoning for Emerging Entities in Temporal Knowledge Graphs
s81a46184d9.description: arXiv:2611.34708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temporal knowledge graphs (TKGs) continually introduce emerging entities whose interaction histories evolve from zero-shot debuts into sparse, bursty few-shot trajectories. However, current paradigms are fragmented: pattern-transfer methods lack catalog-wide event memory, whereas online memory models suffer from endpoint-role asymmetry that degrades unseen-answer ranking. s81a46184d9.summary: INSPIRE is a two-stage reasoning method for predicting interactions of emerging entities in temporal knowledge graphs, addressing sparse, bursty few-shot histories.

s29107442cb.title: What Is a Theory Worth to an LLM Solver? Measuring, Inducing, and Merging Theories in Context
s29107442cb.description: arXiv:2611.34751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mathematicians solve problems faster when they know the right theory. s29107442cb.why: Suggests structured domain theory in prompts can outperform extra examples for solver accuracy and token efficiency, though the gain shrinks as models and budgets grow.

seee7245816.title: TASK Memory: Beyond Text-Only Memory with Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing against Memory Hallucination
seee7245816.description: arXiv:2611.34762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on external memory, yet they still hallucinate about what they remember. seee7245816.why: Agent builders relying on retrieval memory need to know that correct retrieved facts can still be ignored or misapplied due to conflicts with parametric knowledge.

s5b8ba2ac82.title: Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent: Self-Structuring Learning through Question Answering
s5b8ba2ac82.description: arXiv:2611.34841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of constructing knowledge bases for applications based on large language models, in which the structure of a knowledge base determines how an application can retrieve and connect the information needed to answer a question. s5b8ba2ac82.why: Offers a possible approach for building retrieval-backed LLM applications where the knowledge base structure is learned from question-answer feedback.

s3c89154072.title: Show Your Work: Can Small Open Models Read SEC Filings with Evidence a Machine Can Check?
s3c89154072.description: arXiv:2611.24990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A fluent answer from a language model is not a verified one. s3c89154072.why: Gives teams a way to assess whether small local models can produce verifiable, auditable extractions from financial documents.

s4ab332767a.title: Attributing Agentic Failure in Reasoning Vision-Language Models with Interactive 2D Environments
s4ab332767a.description: arXiv:2611.33162v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic benchmarks report a success rate that confounds distinct causes of failure: misreading the environment, never working out how components of the environment operates, operating the components in the wrong order, and failing to recover from a mistake, each of which calls for a different fix.
