s4ab332767a.summary: MultiNet v2.0-Gridworld is an interactive maze benchmark designed to attribute agentic failures in reasoning vision-language models to specific causes rather than just ranking success rates.
s4ab332767a.why: Separating perception, mechanism understanding, ordering, and recovery failures helps engineers target the right fix for agent failures.

s820a650720.title: Quantum Machine Learning for Signature Forgery Detection
s820a650720.description: arXiv:2611.33163v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Offline handwritten signatures remain a primary behavioural biometric in legal and financial documents. Detecting skilled forgeries from a static raster image is hard because pen pressure, timing and stroke order are missing. This work studies a family of quantum machine learning pipelines for offline signature forgery detection on a public Kaggle corpus of images split into two classes. We pair a ZZ feature map quantum kernel with three classical learners: K-Nearest Neighbours, Support Vector Machine and Random Forest. We then propose a deeper hybrid that uses EfficientNetB0 as a frozen feature extractor, reduces the resulting 1280 dimensional representation to a qubit register sized subspace through a quantum compatible principal componen
s820a650720.summary: The paper studies quantum machine learning pipelines pairing a ZZ feature map quantum kernel with classical learners for offline signature forgery detection on a Kaggle image dataset.

s766b6b8128.title: Psychophysics of Duration Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
s766b6b8128.description: arXiv:2611.33176v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Studies of time perception in language models focus mainly on text-based settings. Yet multimodal models are increasingly used for tasks that require perceiving the passage of time, making the limits of their temporal perception important to understand. We measure the limits of duration perception from audio against a human baseline to address this gap. Drawing from psychophysics, we operationalise duration perception as a melody recognition task, testing when a melody becomes unrecognisable as it is slowed down. Of 21 tested models, most cannot recognise well-known melodies without labelled in-context examples. With in-context examples, seven recognise melodies reliably, most peaking within the median human recognition band. Generalisation
s766b6b8128.summary: A study tests duration perception in 21 multimodal models by asking when slowed-down melodies become unrecognisable, comparing results against a human baseline.
s766b6b8128.why: Shows that most tested audio-capable models struggle with temporal perception, a limit relevant to applications requiring timing judgments from audio.

se2e004cb80.title: Neighbor Crowding Predicts Feature Stability in Sparse Autoencoders
se2e004cb80.description: arXiv:2611.33182v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) offer an approach to identify language model representations by breaking apart polysemantic features into more sparse, interpretable ones. Yet, it is challenging to identify which of the learned features are actually stable, rather than artifacts of initialization. One approach is to train multiple SAE seeds, and compare the learned features across seeds by cosine similarity, but this is notably costly. This raises the question of whether stable features can be identified without the computational expense of training multiple seeds. In this work, we examine cross-seed feature stability across differing levels of training tokens, and demonstrate that in TopK SAEs, it is highly predictable using six computationally
se2e004cb80.summary: The paper examines whether neighbor crowding statistics can identify stable sparse autoencoder features without training multiple costly SAE seeds.
se2e004cb80.why: A cheaper stability check for SAE features could reduce the compute needed for interpretability work on language models.

s8beb4eff22.title: REI: Learning Ideation from Repository Evolution
s8beb4eff22.description: arXiv:2611.33183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As AI systems become increasingly capable of executing and evaluating experiments, ideation is emerging as a bottleneck in automated scientific and engineering iteration. In many real-world domains, useful ideas are sparse and their validation is costly, making direct online exploration inefficient. We observe that repository evolution provides a scalable source of reusable technical experience: code changes record concrete technical hypotheses, while subsequent revisions, adoption, and reuse provide signals about their utility. Based on this observation, we propose REI, a Repository Evolution-driven Ideation framework that learns reusable ideation policies from repository evolution, injecting domain-specific technical experience into model
s8beb4eff22.summary: REI proposes learning ideation for automated research by using repository evolution, where code changes and later revisions signal the utility of technical hypotheses.
s8beb4eff22.why: Suggests a scalable way to train idea generators for automated engineering iteration without costly online experimentation.

s1027e0aa17.title: Semantic Density Does Not Predict Agent-Memory Collapse
s1027e0aa17.description: arXiv:2611.33184v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Persistent textual memory can improve LLM agents, but repeated updates can erode task performance. We ask whether memory-store statistics warn before held-out accuracy declines. We registered mean pairwise cosine similarity ($\rho$) and 13 additional geometry, retrieval, and graph statistics on 805 snapshots from 13 memory methods across ALFWorld, AppWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, and two ARC-AGI settings. These methods store trajectories, rules, workflows, strategies, or linked records, using selective retrieval or whole-store prompting. No such statistic reliably predicted early signs of task accuracy decline, and $\rho$ had zero median lead. With the checkpoint after peak accuracy as a secondary decline point, measures of highly similar p
s1027e0aa17.summary: The paper reports that mean pairwise cosine similarity and 13 other memory-store statistics do not predict held-out accuracy collapse in LLM agent memory across 805 snapshots.
s1027e0aa17.why: Engineers cannot rely on these simple store statistics as early warnings for agent memory degradation, so other monitoring is needed.

s8903612d16.title: Dynamics of Collective Diversity in Human-AI Co-Creation for Creative Tasks
s8903612d16.description: arXiv:2611.33192v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI systems are increasingly deployed at scale to support human users in creative tasks across a variety of domains. However, as more users adopt the same AI agent, the resulting artifacts may become increasingly homogeneous, leading to a collapse in collective diversity. Prior work has documented this risk, but lacks a systematic framework for understanding how collective diversity changes as AI adoption scales across co-creation settings. In this work, we conduct a large-scale crowdsourcing study to understand and model the dynamics of collective diversity, quality, and effort in human-AI co-creation across two creative domains: Creative Hypothesis Generation and Creative Story Writing. We find that current AI agents used in co-
s8903612d16.summary: A large crowdsourcing study models how collective diversity in human-AI co-creation changes as more users adopt the same generative AI agent.
s8903612d16.why: Shows that widespread AI tool adoption may homogenize creative outputs, a risk for product designers of creative tools.

sb1d624b2fe.title: Formalization, Transparency, and Collusion in Open-Source Game Theory
sb1d624b2fe.description: arXiv:2611.33193v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cooperation among AI agents will undermine alignment protocols when it takes the form of collusion. Under these protocols, agents often have some information about one another, and how much they have may determine whether they collude. Open-source game theory studies the extreme case, in which each program reads its opponent's source code and acts based on what it can prove about it. We develop formal foundations for this theory: we specify a concrete proof system, resolve an open problem concerning DupocBot and CupodBot through a transposition argument, and mechanize the framework in Lean 4; to our knowledge, this is the first mechanization of resource-bounded open-source game theory. We then extend the framework to the more realistic sett
sb1d624b2fe.summary: The paper formalizes open-source game theory, specifying a proof system and resolving an open problem about DupocBot and CupodBot, with implications for AI agent collusion.
sb1d624b2fe.why: Clarifies when agents that read each other's source code can prove cooperative behavior, relevant to alignment protocols against collusion.

s4a06690698.title: Verified experience improves materials prediction with large language models
s4a06690698.description: arXiv:2611.33195v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Materials discovery is an iterative loop: experiments and calculations verify predictions, and each outcome can inform the next. Yet most predictors are specialized single-task models fixed after training. Large language models have recently emerged as predictors across heterogeneous tasks but generally underperform specialized models, and retrieval-augmented variants discard their own outcomes. Benchmarks also score queries in isolation, leaving improvement from outcomes untested. Here we construct MatMemBench, a sequential benchmark of 22 materials tasks that reveals outcomes only after prediction and tests online adaptation, memory retention and cross-task transfer. We present MatRecall, a framework that lets large language models store
s4a06690698.summary: MatMemBench is a sequential benchmark of 22 materials prediction tasks testing whether LLM predictors improve when they can use verified outcomes from earlier queries.
s4a06690698.why: Introduces a way to measure whether LLMs learn from verified feedback over time, rather than scoring each query in isolation.

sa1266fb70a.title: Extraneous Cognitive Load in Large Language Models
sa1266fb70a.description: arXiv:2611.33197v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) shows that human problem-solving is affected by both intrinsic load, arising from task difficulty, and extraneous load, arising from how task information is presented. Large language models (LLMs) show analogous effects: presentation alone can affect model performance, but these effects have not yet been systematically isolated from task difficulty. To address this gap, we introduce CogLoadBench, a controlled benchmark that varies five CLT-inspired presentation factors across three reasoning task families. Across models, we find that higher extraneous load conditions often reduce accuracy by either adding competition or complicating the reasoning path. To support diagnosis and mitigation of load-related effects,
sa1266fb70a.summary: CogLoadBench is a benchmark that varies five cognitive-load-inspired presentation factors across three reasoning task families to isolate extraneous load effects in LLMs.
sa1266fb70a.why: Shows that how a task is presented can affect model performance independently of difficulty, which matters for prompt design.

s5c10d3ec27.title: UniMoE-CP: Unified Conditional Waveform Prediction Across Measured Optical Wireless Links
s5c10d3ec27.description: arXiv:2611.33198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Shared prediction across measured optical wireless links requires a common model to accommodate link-dependent waveform dynamics. This paper studies unified learning for underwater optical, 100-m visible-light communication and 4.3-km free-space optical links. We formulate received-waveform forecasting from historical observations and known future transmitted excitation using one shared parameter set. UniMoE-CP combines a shared pool of temporal experts, window-dependent routing and spectral covariate fusion with an autoregressive decoder. The design permits conditional specialization while reusing expert parameters across the measured links. Pooled-training benchmarks evaluate each link separately and report an aggregated result using norm
s5c10d3ec27.summary: UniMoE-CP is a unified mixture-of-experts model that forecasts received waveforms across underwater optical, 100-m visible-light, and 4.3-km free-space optical links using one parameter set.

saae252d93f.title: The AI Disclosure Paradox: Operational Disclosure and the Rise of Corporate AI Narratives
saae252d93f.description: arXiv:2611.33201v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI-related corporate disclosure can expand while becoming less concentrated on current use. Across U.S. SEC filings from 2017 to 2025, AI-related passage intensity increased 6.3-fold between 2017-2022 and 2023-2025, whereas corrected operational-disclosure intensity increased 3.3-fold. The operational share fell from 25.76% to 13.45%; approximately 89% of the net increase in passage intensity fell outside the operational category. The decline persists within sectors and filing types and in 10-K-only analysis. These estimates combine frozen language-model predictions for 26,279 AI-related passages with an audit of 1,000 annotated passages. The findings distinguish growth in organizational attention from growth in implementation-specific clai
saae252d93f.summary: An arXiv paper analyzing U.S. SEC filings from 2017 to 2025 finds AI-related disclosure grew sharply but became less focused on operational use.
saae252d93f.why: Suggests corporate AI claims in filings increasingly describe narratives rather than deployed operations, which matters for due diligence on AI capability claims.

sa59264ab22.title: How Many Samples Is RL Worth? Best-of-N versus RL Post-Training for Text-to-Image Models
sa59264ab22.description: arXiv:2611.33232v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) on a reward that can be checked automatically has become a common last step in the training of text-to-image models. A simpler way to get more correct images is best-of-N: draw N images from the base model and keep the one that a picker prefers. We ask how many base model samples one RL sample is worth, and call this number the exchange rate. We measure it for Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium and its public Flow-GRPO checkpoint on 398 new prompts in the style of GenEval, the benchmark behind the RL reward, with human labels on every prompt and two automatic judges other than the reward. The answer depends on the prompt. Four fifths of the prompts do not ask for a position (for example, one object left of another). On
sa59264ab22.summary: A paper measures how many best-of-N base-model samples equal one RL post-training sample for Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium and its Flow-GRPO checkpoint.
sa59264ab22.why: Gives teams a concrete way to compare the cost of best-of-N sampling against RL post-training for text-to-image models.

s6497a83f2d.title: Diagnostically Meaningful, Privacy-aware Synthetic Chest CT via Class-Conditional Latent Sampling in Diffusion Autoencoders
s6497a83f2d.description: arXiv:2611.33234v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large, well-annotated datasets are essential for developing medical artificial intelligence models, yet data sharing is often restricted by privacy regulations. Synthetic images may help address this limitation if they preserve diagnostic information while reducing the risk of reproducing patient data. We developed a diffusion autoencoder-based framework for class-conditional synthetic chest CT generation that incorporates latent-space distance filtering to reduce the likelihood of regenerating training samples. A diffusion autoencoder was trained on the public RSNA 2020 Pulmonary Embolism (PE) dataset. PE-positive and PE-negative images were synthesized by sampling latent representations from class-specific kernel density estimates. Sample
s6497a83f2d.summary: Researchers present a diffusion autoencoder framework that generates class-conditional synthetic chest CT images, filtering out samples close to training data to reduce privacy risk.
s6497a83f2d.why: Offers a possible route to sharing medical imaging training data under privacy constraints, though the text gives limited detail on results.

s12158cf89a.title: KiRA: Kronecker Input-Gated Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Pretrained Models
s12158cf89a.description: arXiv:2611.33236v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Full fine-tuning of large pretrained models is expensive, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) is the standard alternative. Most PEFT methods use low-rank updates, whose rank lies far below that of full fine-tuning and is the same for every input. Input-adaptive variants vary the capacity per input but remain within the low-rank bottleneck, and whether a task benefits from input conditioning is not known before training. This paper introduces Kronecker input-gated rank adaptation (KiRA). s12158cf89a.summary: The paper introduces KiRA, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that replaces the low-rank product with an input-gated Kronecker structure.
s12158cf89a.why: Proposes a fine-tuning alternative that may achieve input-adaptive capacity beyond standard low-rank methods, though the text gives no benchmark results.

sb6042980c6.title: Sequential Testing on Complex and High Dimensional Data Streams Leveraging Unsupervised Model Errors
sb6042980c6.description: arXiv:2611.33238v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose two general, distribution-free test statistics for binary Sequential Hypothesis Testing (SHT) and Sequential Change Point Detection (SCPD) respectively, in streaming environments where the data (e.g., network traffic metadata) are too complicated for the exact probabilistic modeling required by conventional likelihood ratio-driven tests. Our framework also addresses the challenge of information asymmetry, where data is available only from the null/pre-change regime and not from the alternative/post-change one such as zero-day attacks or emerging disease related regimes. The proposed statistics monitor the errors of a predictive or reconstructive machine learning model trained solely on null/pre-change data, relying on imperfect g
sb6042980c6.summary: Researchers propose distribution-free test statistics for sequential hypothesis testing and change point detection on streaming data using unsupervised model errors.
sb6042980c6.why: Could help detect anomalies such as zero-day attacks in network streams when only normal-regime data is available.

s70764e24a9.title: CypherMAS: Benchmarking Routing Reliability in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
s70764e24a9.description: arXiv:2611.33242v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs) distribute reasoning across specialized agents that must exchange messages and invoke tools reliably. Existing evaluations typically couple communication with open domain tasks, making it difficult to determine whether a failure arises from reasoning, malformed tool use, lost messages, or forgotten requests. Prior benchmarks do not isolate communication execution or measure routing redundancy against a known optimal path. We introduce CypherMAS, a synthetic benchmark that isolates communication and routing in fixed multi-agent graphs. s70764e24a9.summary: CypherMAS is a synthetic benchmark that isolates communication and routing reliability in LLM-based multi-agent systems, separate from open-domain reasoning tasks.
s70764e24a9.why: Helps engineers diagnose whether multi-agent failures come from messaging or tool routing rather than reasoning.

sba37651d6e.title: Beyond the Efficiency-Efficacy Dilemma: A Critical Analysis of Transferability in Adversarial Malware Detection
sba37651d6e.description: arXiv:2611.33243v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine Learning (ML) models are already being deployed at scale for malware detection. Therefore there is a pressing need to rigorously study adversarial robustness. To that end, we introduce the Adversarial AI Engine (AAIE): a platform for automated security stress-testing. We performed transfer attacks, via EMBER2018, against a Random Forest target. Counterintuitively, we found single-step FGSM to have the highest attack success rate (ASR) of 52.9% compared to iterative PGD with 45.2% (p < 0.002). Compared to iterative attacks which tend to overfit surrogate networks creating brittle perturbations, FGSM created more transferable examples. sba37651d6e.summary: Researchers introduce the Adversarial AI Engine for stress-testing malware detectors and report transfer attacks against a Random Forest model using EMBER2018.
sba37651d6e.why: Shows that simpler single-step attacks can outperform iterative ones against deployed ML malware detectors, relevant to security evaluation practices.

s15d8153013.title: Anti-AI in the Wild: From Toxic Discourse to Action
s15d8153013.description: arXiv:2611.33254v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online discussion of generative AI has become increasingly contentious, and communities devoted to supporting, opposing, or debating AI have emerged on social media. Some of these communities take anti-AI actions, such as deploying crawler tarpits and data-poisoning services to interfere with data collection and model training. Yet, the scope of these actions and their relationship to online discourse remain poorly understood. In this paper, we present the first measurement study of online conflict over generative AI, from toxic discourse to anti-AI actions. We collect 931,640 posts from 25 Reddit communities, label them with a large language model detector validated against human labels, identify 3,312 anti-AI actions, and trace the output
s15d8153013.summary: A measurement study examines online conflict over generative AI, tracing toxic discourse to anti-AI actions such as crawler tarpits and data-poisoning services.
s15d8153013.why: Highlights organized resistance tactics like data poisoning that could affect data collection and training pipelines.

s49088bcf7e.title: One Token, Many Lessons: Sliding-Window Attention within Gated Delta Networks
s49088bcf7e.description: arXiv:2611.33257v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Linear attention compresses historical context into a fixed-size recurrent state, reducing the computational and memory costs of long-sequence modeling. From the perspective of test-time regression (TTR), the state matrix can be viewed as an online-learned regression model, where keys and values serve as inputs and targets respectively, and queries are used to read from the model. From this perspective, the effectiveness of state learning depends not only on the update rule but also on how the key-value learning pairs used for state updates are constructed. s49088bcf7e.summary: A paper proposes sliding-window attention within gated delta networks to improve linear attention's state learning for long-sequence modeling.
s49088bcf7e.why: Offers an architectural variant for efficient long-context models, though the text provides no performance figures.

sba5c870601.title: Onnx2TEE: Automated Graph-Aware Model Partitioning for TEE-based Edge AI Protection
sba5c870601.description: arXiv:2611.33262v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI models are increasingly being deployed at the edge. Since these models often require significant research and development to produce, are often deployed in potentially hostile environments, and downstream systems often rely on accurate data; protecting them from theft or manipulation is worthy of serious consideration. Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), which provide hardware-enforced separation of software execution, can protect model weights but impose strict resource constraints, making full-model execution impractical for large neural networks. We present Onnx2TEE, an automated, model-independent pipeline that partitions ONNX models across rich, trusted execution environments for non-sequential feed-forward networks using graph-a
sba5c870601.summary: Onnx2TEE is a graph-aware model partitioning approach that splits edge AI models to run within trusted execution environments under memory constraints.
sba5c870601.why: Addresses protecting proprietary edge model weights from theft or tampering while working within TEE resource limits.

s285745fc49.title: A Hierarchy of Risk Certificates for Representation-Based Prediction
s285745fc49.description: arXiv:2611.33333v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Representation-based prediction underlies many machine-learning systems. Yet a fitted predictor's failure to meet an accuracy requirement does not establish that its representation-decoder class cannot meet it. We study optimal population mean squared error (MSE) over Lipschitz decoders acting on a fixed representation. For blocks of $b\geq2$ independent and identically distributed (iid) observations, we minimize total squared error (normalized by $b-1$) under pairwise Lipschitz constraints. We prove that expected block scores form nondecreasing lower bounds on optimal class risk and converge to that risk on compact metric feature spaces, although no fixed block size provides a uniform relative guarantee. s285745fc49.summary: The paper studies optimal population mean squared error over Lipschitz decoders on fixed representations and derives a hierarchy of risk certificates.

s6bcbd37e56.title: Benchmarking Segmentation Models for Scalable Mangrove Mapping with Sentinel-1/2 Imagery
s6bcbd37e56.description: arXiv:2611.33369v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mangroves are dynamic coastal ecosystems that contribute to carbon storage, coastal protection and biodiversity conservation, but are vulnerable to climate change. Very-high-resolution imagery such as Pl\'eiades enables detailed mangrove mapping but it is costly and have a low revisit rate. Large-scale monitoring requires free and regularly available data such as Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 but their spatial resolution poses challenges for detailed mangrove mapping. In this work, we benchmark deep learning approaches for mangrove mapping from Sentinel-1 radar and Sentinel-2 optical imagery using reference maps derived from very-high-resolution Pl\'eiades imagery. We compare four segmentation configurations based on CROMA and BigEarthNet-pretr
s6bcbd37e56.summary: Researchers benchmark deep learning segmentation models for mangrove mapping using free Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellite imagery.
s6bcbd37e56.why: Shows how freely available satellite data can support scalable ecological monitoring compared with costly high-resolution imagery.

sed35a45a71.title: Poisoning Self-Evolving Security Policies in LLM Agents
sed35a45a71.description: arXiv:2611.33385v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-evolving defenses improve LLM-agent security by learning reusable policies from observed attacks. However, we demonstrate that this learning process itself can become an attack surface. Using SED (Self-Evolving Defense) in the AgentDojo benchmark, we construct a single prompt-injection episode that causes the defense to learn an over-broad policy and subsequently refuse legitimate requests. Across 10 Nemotron runs, every poisoned run over-refuses at least one legitimate task, while unrelated-task performance remains unchanged and the original prompt-injection defense remains effective. sed35a45a71.summary: Researchers show that the learning process of a self-evolving defense in LLM agents can be poisoned via a single prompt-injection episode, causing over-refusal of legitimate tasks.
sed35a45a71.why: Shows that adaptive security policies learned from attacks can themselves become an attack surface, which matters for agent deployments.

sf354f7554c.title: RoboARC: Physical Puzzles for Robotic Manipulation under Spatial Constraints
sf354f7554c.description: arXiv:2611.33390v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many hard manipulation tasks come down to a spatial constraint that only a few motions satisfy, such as passing a part through a gap barely wider than itself or separating two interlocked parts. These motions depend on the exact geometry of each scene, so demonstrations and skills recorded elsewhere rarely transfer. We therefore ask: when manipulation hinges on spatial constraints, can robots reason out the right motions? We introduce RoboARC, a benchmark of 90 tasks in six constraint types over rigid and soft materials, on three robots in MuJoCo. sf354f7554c.summary: RoboARC is a benchmark of 90 robotic manipulation tasks requiring spatial-constraint reasoning across rigid and soft materials, tested on three robots in simulation.
sf354f7554c.why: Provides a testbed for whether robots can reason about geometry-specific motions instead of relying on transferred demonstrations.

s8593cef743.title: Best-of-$N$ Test-Time Steering Can Lead to Reward Hacking in Vision-Language-Action Models
s8593cef743.description: arXiv:2611.33398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise for general-purpose robotic manipulation, but adapting to changing environmental conditions still remains challenging. Recent test-time steering methods have shown promise in enabling adaptive VLA policies by utilizing additional computation during deployment. In this paper, we consider best-of-$N$ test-time steering for VLA models, where multiple action candidates are sampled from a fixed policy and a verifier is used to select the best one during deployment. s8593cef743.summary: The paper shows that best-of-N test-time steering for vision-language-action robot models can lead to reward hacking as N increases.
s8593cef743.why: Warns that scaling verifier-based action selection at deployment can degrade behavior by exploiting the verifier, a risk for robot policy engineers.

s5e908676b6.title: Sequentially Acquiring Concept Knowledge to Guide Continual Learning
s5e908676b6.description: arXiv:2611.33399v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The goal of continual learning (CL) is to adapt to new data (plasticity) while retaining the knowledge acquired from old data (stability). Existing methods are explicitly designed to focus on balancing stability and plasticity to mitigate the challenge of catastrophic forgetting while promoting learning. However, the impact of order and nature of samples from the new data that the network is trained on remains an under explored factor. We argue that a CL algorithm should have the ability to rank incoming samples in terms of their relationship with prior data and their effect on the learning process. s5e908676b6.summary: Researchers propose a continual learning approach that ranks incoming samples by their relationship to existing knowledge, studying how sample order and nature affect stability and plasticity.
s5e908676b6.why: Sample ordering in continual training is an under-explored factor that could affect how models retain old knowledge while learning new data.

s61dd4058af.title: Temporal Selective Exploration for Reinforcement Learning-Guided Continuous-Discrete Flow Matching in 3D Molecular Design
s61dd4058af.description: arXiv:2611.33417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Flow matching has shown strong potential in generative tasks, while its optimization via Reinforcement Learning (RL) remains underexplored, especially in continuous-discrete mixed settings. Moreover, flow matching is formulated as an Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE), whose deterministic trajectories do not naturally support RL optimization. Introducing stochasticity by converting the entire trajectory into a Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) is a common practice. Nevertheless, not all timesteps contribute to the final outcomes, and redundant exploration introduces additional noise. s61dd4058af.summary: Researchers apply reinforcement learning to continuous-discrete flow matching for 3D molecular design, selectively exploring timesteps when converting ODE trajectories to SDEs.

se452d5cd8e.title: When the Knowledge Runs Out: A Part-Level Pilot Evaluation of How Language Models Handle Partially Covered Questions
se452d5cd8e.description: arXiv:2611.33428v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Assistants that answer from supplied reference material often receive material that covers some parts of a user's question and not others. Existing evaluations of insufficient context mostly score one answer per question, and often treat partially sufficient context as simply insufficient. We describe a small, open evaluation that scores each part of a three-part question separately, with a verdict for parts that are answered correctly from the material but carry an added unsupported claim. On 30 cases (five scenarios, six coverage patterns, five samples each) we test claude-haiku-4-5 and llama3.1:8b. se452d5cd8e.summary: Researchers release a small open evaluation scoring each part of three-part questions separately when reference material only partially covers them.
se452d5cd8e.why: Per-part scoring exposes failures that single-answer evaluations miss when supplied context is only partially sufficient.

sbc50749613.title: HumblePRM: Improving VLM Abstention in Ambiguous Situations through Process Reward Modeling
sbc50749613.description: arXiv:2611.33452v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reliable deployment of Vision Language Models (VLMs) requires that a model's expressed confidence remain grounded in what it can actually see, and that it recognize when the visual evidence is too ambiguous to commit to a confident response. Standard post-training uses outcome reward models (ORMs) that supervise only the final decision, rewarding a confident answer regardless of whether the image supports one, while existing methods either tend to detect uncertainty post-hoc or assume an objective verdict always exists. sbc50749613.summary: HumblePRM uses process reward modeling to teach vision language models to abstain when visual evidence is too ambiguous, instead of rewarding confident answers regardless of image support.
sbc50749613.why: Reliable VLM deployment needs confidence grounded in visual evidence, and outcome-only reward models can reward overconfident answers.

s427d8bb5d0.title: SecID: An LLM-Guided Framework for Threat-Aware Secondary Asset Identification with Quantitative RTL Analysis
s427d8bb5d0.description: arXiv:2611.33453v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The growing complexity of modern hardware designs is making security assurance increasingly difficult. One of the foundational steps in pre-silicon security verification is identifying security assets. While primary assets are often evident from design functionality, the internal signals that can facilitate their compromise are much less apparent. Complex data- and control-flow dependencies create many such internal security-critical locations, whose exploitation depends on the threat-specific attack mechanism---these are the secondary assets. To precisely identify these, we propose SecID, a multi-agent framework that combines deterministic RTL analysis with bounded dynamic evaluation and LLM reasoning to identify threat-specific secondary
s427d8bb5d0.summary: SecID is an LLM-guided framework for identifying secondary security assets in RTL hardware designs, combined with quantitative RTL analysis.
s427d8bb5d0.why: Pre-silicon security verification teams could use automated secondary asset identification to find internal signals that enable compromise.

sbf40509517.title: Benchmarking Open-Ended Vulnerability Discovery in Windows Kernel Binaries
sbf40509517.description: arXiv:2611.33486v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Frontier models are increasingly used to discover real-world security vulnerabilities, making it critical to systematically evaluate their cybersecurity capabilities. However, existing security benchmarks primarily focus on known vulnerabilities in open-source projects, largely overlooking closed-source binaries, which underpin much of the software industry. In this paper, we ask: how effective are frontier models at uncovering deep vulnerabilities in production binaries? To answer this question, we present DeepBinary, the first comprehensive benchmark for open-ended vulnerability discovery in Windows kernel binaries. Given a target binary, an agent analyzes it using a disassembler and kernel debugger in network-isolated VMs and reports eac
sbf40509517.summary: DeepBinary is a benchmark testing how well frontier models find deep, unknown vulnerabilities in closed-source Windows kernel binaries rather than known open-source flaws.
sbf40509517.why: Closed-source binaries underpin much of the industry, and this benchmark targets vulnerability discovery where existing security benchmarks have little coverage.

s750faf8dff.title: The Geometry Is the Memory: Task-Density Routing for Continual LoRA
s750faf8dff.description: arXiv:2611.33487v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Freezing older adapters does not ensure that a continual learner will select and use them properly at inference time. When multiple adapters exist, routing among them and identifying the adapter whose representation space matches the query's answer can be difficult. We propose CONTLORA, which replaces stored examples with compact class statistics for adapter selection and classification. Gaussian class models in a frozen representation select LoRA adapters, while accumulated feature moments exactly recover a class-balanced ridge classifier for fixed training features. Trained without retaining images or feature vectors, CONTLORA reaches 88.55% accuracy on 20-task CIFAR-100 and 86.99% on CUB-200. Across three benchmarks in the matched compon
s750faf8dff.summary: CONTLORA proposes routing among frozen LoRA adapters using compact class statistics instead of stored examples, selecting adapters via Gaussian class models in a frozen representation.
s750faf8dff.why: Replacing stored examples with compact statistics could simplify continual fine-tuning systems that manage multiple adapters.

sdbd29855dd.title: Joint Estimation of Abilities and Item Parameters for Large Language Models Using Probability and Binary Responses: A Fractional-Response IRT Framework
sdbd29855dd.description: arXiv:2611.33493v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) evaluations provide two response types: probabilities assigned to correct answers and binary indicators of correctness. Restricting evaluation to one type narrows the range of available models or discards probability information. We propose a method to integrate both types through a common two-parameter logistic item response model and fractional-response quasi-maximum likelihood estimation. The framework includes binary-only models in common-scale evaluation without discarding available probabilityinformation; broader measurement coverage does not by itself ensure greater precision or measurement equivalence. Simulations evaluate statistical efficiency when both response types have the same expected value. Moreov
sdbd29855dd.summary: Researchers propose a fractional-response IRT framework that jointly uses probability and binary correctness responses to estimate LLM abilities and item parameters.
sdbd29855dd.why: Combining probability and binary signals could make LLM benchmark comparisons more informative without discarding data.

s1ef4fc7c2f.title: PRECEPT: Security Self-Improvement of Coding Agents via Evolving Principles
s1ef4fc7c2f.description: arXiv:2611.33519v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI coding agents increasingly write and submit code with limited human review, and much of it passes functional tests while remaining insecure. We show that these failures persist. Across 14 task sequences, Codex, Claude Code, and Qwen Code fixed a vulnerability 85.7% of the time when shown the failing security test, then reintroduced the same vulnerability class in a new session 26.7% of the time, about as often as agents that had never seen it (27.5%). The capability is present; the retention is not. Neither recording the repair in the agent's persistent context nor supplying published secure coding principles closed the gap: the recorded fix stayed tied to the family of the task it came from, and the principles, written for human develop
s1ef4fc7c2f.summary: PRECEPT proposes evolving security principles for coding agents, after finding agents reintroduced fixed vulnerability classes in new sessions 26.7% of the time.
s1ef4fc7c2f.why: Coding agents that reintroduce fixed vulnerabilities across sessions show that recorded repairs alone do not preserve security retention.

sca7c4ef13e.title: RankCast: Phase-Aware Rank Balancing in MoE Serving
sca7c4ef13e.description: arXiv:2611.33542v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern large language model (LLM) inference increasingly adopts disaggregated architectures that separate Prefill (P) and Decode (D) phases. Meanwhile, Expert Parallelism (EP) has been widely adopted in large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model serving. However, load imbalance still slows down MoE inference because each layer must wait for the busiest EP rank. The main source of latency differs between prefill and decode. Prefill is compute-bound, and its MoE layers' latency is determined by the maximum token count of the busiest rank. At the same time, under moderate batch sizes, Decode is memory-bound, so the latency is dominated by the maximum active-expert count across ranks. To solve both problems under a unified framework, we present RankC
sca7c4ef13e.summary: RankCast proposes phase-aware rank balancing for serving Mixture-of-Experts models, addressing load imbalance across expert parallelism ranks in prefill and decode phases.
sca7c4ef13e.why: Expert load imbalance slows MoE inference, and phase-specific balancing targets different latency sources in prefill and decode.

s0d16ad717e.title: DexEngine: Scaling Human Demonstrations into Physically Executable Whole-Robot Data
s0d16ad717e.description: arXiv:2611.33579v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A growing body of recent work addresses the retargeting of human hand-object demonstrations to robotic hands. To train whole-robot policies, however, the retargeted motions must be kinematically feasible and physically executable, and be produced efficiently at scale. We present DexEngine, a simulation pipeline that turns human manipulation data into train-ready, physically executable arm-hand trajectories. DexEngine first places each clip's hand-object motion where the arms can reach it, finds an arm motion that follows the human hands, and then corrects the motion in physics simulation with residual reinforcement learning. From nine human hand-object datasets, we generate about 5,200 clips for each of four dexterous hands, augmented into
s0d16ad717e.summary: DexEngine is a simulation pipeline that converts human hand-object demonstrations into physically executable arm-hand trajectories for training whole-robot policies at scale.

sc0e894dfe2.title: The Detour Is the Danger: Preserving Security During LLM Agent Recovery
sc0e894dfe2.description: arXiv:2611.33605v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on external tools and reusable Skills to execute complex workflows, autonomously replanning when operations fail. However, such recovery may preserve task functionality while silently discarding the security protections required by the original workflow. In this paper, we investigate workflow security downgrade, a failure-induced security threat in which agents execute sensitive operations without satisfying their original protection requirements. Unlike prompt injection, this threat exploits autonomous recovery decisions triggered by execution failures, without modifying instructions or tool definitions. We systematically evaluate this behavior through fault injection in an executable MCP/Skill environment span
sc0e894dfe2.summary: Researchers identify workflow security downgrade, where LLM agents replanning after failures drop security protections of the original workflow while still completing tasks.
sc0e894dfe2.why: Autonomous recovery in agents can silently discard security requirements, a risk distinct from prompt injection that engineers building agent workflows must address.

s53b75ed3cc.title: What Is Redundant at High Resolution? Efficient Attention and Feed-Forward Design for All-in-One Image Restoration
s53b75ed3cc.description: arXiv:2611.33636v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-scale architectures are widely adopted in all-in-one image restoration (AIO-IR) to capture larger-scale context at low-resolution stages and refine details at high-resolution (HR) stages. However, processing spatially large feature maps at HR stages incurs substantial computational costs and memory traffic, making efficient HR processing challenging. To address this challenge, we propose High-resolution Global-Local Restoration (HiGLR), an efficient multi-scale AIO-IR network grounded in an analysis of spatial redundancy in self-attention and convolutional feed-forward networks (ConvFFNs). Specifically, this analysis identifies three key redundancies: per-query readout at the finest-scale stage, key routing across neighboring queries
s53b75ed3cc.summary: HiGLR is an efficient multi-scale all-in-one image restoration network that reduces high-resolution processing costs based on an analysis of spatial redundancy in self-attention.

se56b221d5f.title: Read Before You Use: Improving Visual Memory Utilization in Vision-Language Models
se56b221d5f.description: arXiv:2611.33687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal memory enables long-horizon vision-language agents to preserve and retrieve past experiences. While prior research has focused on memory construction and retrieval, effectively using the provided memory remains a challenge for vision-language models (VLMs). We find that VLMs often fail to answer downstream questions even when sufficient multimodal evidence is provided. To investigate why VLMs struggle, we replace memory images with reference captions and observe substantial performance gains, suggesting difficulties in reading visual evidence directly. However, model-generated captions may omit critical information, limiting this approach in practice. These limitations motivate a closer examination of memory utilization, revealin
se56b221d5f.summary: Researchers find vision-language models often fail to use provided visual memory, and replacing memory images with reference captions substantially improves performance.
se56b221d5f.why: Agents relying on multimodal memory may underperform even when correct evidence is supplied, pointing to a gap in how VLMs read visual memory.

sb90afa7ec3.title: Rethinking Sequential Locate-Then-Edit: Optimality and Stability
sb90afa7ec3.description: arXiv:2611.33692v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Locate-Then-Edit framework enables efficient knowledge updates in large language models without requiring full retraining. Recent research has increasingly focused on sequential editing, where knowledge arrives continuously and the model is updated incrementally. However, existing sequential methods commonly suffer from catastrophic forgetting and model collapse after only a few hundred edits. In contrast, batch editing - which jointly optimizes all edits and yields the optimal solution under a specified editing objective - can support tens of thousands of edits with high edit efficacy while preserving the model's general capabilities, resulting in a substantial performance gap between the two editing paradigms. In this paper, we demons
sb90afa7ec3.summary: Researchers revisit sequential Locate-Then-Edit knowledge editing for LLMs, analyzing why sequential methods collapse after a few hundred edits while batch editing scales further.
sb90afa7ec3.why: Sequential knowledge edits that collapse after a few hundred updates limit maintaining LLMs without retraining, so stability findings matter for update pipelines.

s8c845277bd.title: Sports Agent: A Self-Evolving System for Conversational Data Analytics
s8c845277bd.description: arXiv:2611.33700v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conversational sports analytics requires accurate, evidence-based responses with low latency. Changes in query distributions, data resources, and model behavior can degrade static agent configurations, motivating controlled evolution guided by runtime evidence. We present Sports Agent, a self-evolving framework integrating an Agentic SQL Model for structured-data reasoning, a harness for planning and tool orchestration, and a unified Feedback Engine connecting online execution with offline evolution. The engine assesses responses and execution trajectories, verifies factual claims, diagnoses failures, and generates evolution signals. Model evolution combines SQL-to-Question Scaling for coverage expansion with Graph-Guided Scaling for error-
s8c845277bd.summary: Researchers present Sports Agent, a self-evolving framework for conversational sports analytics combining an Agentic SQL Model, a planning harness, and a Feedback Engine.
s8c845277bd.why: Shows a pattern for keeping data agents accurate over time by using runtime execution feedback to guide controlled offline evolution.

s065fab91ee.title: Practice Makes Fluent: Learning to Use Earlier Predictions in Looped Models
s065fab91ee.description: arXiv:2611.33722v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: People become faster at a task through practice, but models that improve with experience do not necessarily learn to use less computation. We train looped models, whose intermediate predictions allow earlier exits, to perform tasks with fewer iterations through practice. This is difficult because shared-weight updates can degrade the final-loop prediction while improving early ones, and the exit gate must track early predictions as their quality changes. s065fab91ee.summary: Researchers propose FLUENT, a method that trains looped models to use earlier intermediate predictions so they exit early and use less computation on tasks.
s065fab91ee.why: Could help teams cut inference compute by letting models learn to stop iterating once early predictions are good enough.

sf4b893f6ba.title: FlashProve-Next: Verifiable Inference for Production LLM APIs
sf4b893f6ba.description: arXiv:2611.33741v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Clients of closed-weight LLM APIs cannot verify whether a provider ran the advertised model, precision, hidden prompt, and reasoning budget. Existing approaches either trust hardware or third parties, or re-prove every layer of an integer surrogate at high cost while diverging from native floating-point serving. FlashProve-Next produces verifiable, zero-knowledge-masked proofs for individual LLM API responses without modifying native serving (bf16/fp8/mxfp4, random sampling, FlashAttention, CUDA graphs, batching, prefix caching) and without disclosing weights, hidden prompts, hidden reasoning, or activations (dense profiles fix coarse geometry; cross-architecture hiding is deferred). A non-depleting Reed-Solomon weight commitment model_id o
sf4b893f6ba.summary: FlashProve-Next proposes zero-knowledge-masked proofs that let clients verify individual responses from closed-weight LLM APIs ran the advertised model and settings.
sf4b893f6ba.why: Addresses trust in third-party LLM APIs by offering verification of model, precision, and reasoning budget without changing native serving.

s3c638ee3c3.title: Teaching Students to Stand on Their Own: Distilling Vision Foundation Models for Fine-Grained Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning
s3c638ee3c3.description: arXiv:2611.33749v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fine-grained few-shot class-incremental learning (FG-FSCIL) aims to incrementally learn visually similar new classes from limited images without catastrophic forgetting. Prior work typically learns strong representations on base classes or leverages vision foundation models (VFMs) directly as backbones or via knowledge distillation. However, VFM backbones incur high computational costs and do not guarantee fine-grained recognition. Although knowledge distillation reduces inference cost, our preliminary experiments reveal that distilled students still lag substantially behind their VFM teachers, particularly on new classes. To address this limitation, we propose STAND, a systematic VFM-to-student distillation design tailored for FG-FSCIL. Sp
s3c638ee3c3.summary: Researchers study distilling vision foundation models into smaller students for fine-grained few-shot class-incremental learning, noting distilled students struggle with fine-grained recognition.
s3c638ee3c3.why: Relevant to teams deploying compact vision models that must learn new fine-grained classes from few images.

sb1b37bf34d.title: ScanAR: Parallel Row-Scan Decoding for Efficient Image Generation in Unified Autoregressive Models
sb1b37bf34d.description: arXiv:2611.33761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Unified multimodal autoregressive (AR) models represent text and images in one token sequence and generate all modalities with a shared next-token prediction head. Their image generation, however, decodes an $H\times W$ visual grid token by token in raster order, which takes $HW$ sequential steps and dominates inference time. Existing acceleration methods for visual AR generation either change the tokenizer, the prediction head, or the model interface, or keep the model but cannot reach high parallelism without losing quality, so they do not carry over to unified AR models. sb1b37bf34d.summary: ScanAR proposes parallel row-scan decoding to speed up image generation in unified autoregressive multimodal models without changing the tokenizer or prediction head.
sb1b37bf34d.why: Targets the dominant inference bottleneck of sequential raster-order image token decoding in unified multimodal models.

s93a086adfc.title: Triage Before Fine-Tuning: Feasibility-Gated Selection and Monitored Adaptation of Embodied Foundation Models for a Fixed Physical Platform
s93a086adfc.description: arXiv:2611.33772v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Embodied foundation models are increasingly deployed by selection: a practitioner picks a public checkpoint by benchmark rank and fine-tunes it on local data. The platform is fixed before the model is chosen, with little or no local data. We ask what such a checkpoint loses on a fixed platform and which part of the loss local data can buy back. We split the gap by what can repair it. A sensing gap, information the sensors do not capture, cannot be closed with their data; a latency gap, output arriving after the control loop needs it, belongs to the loop, not the weights; only a distribution gap is fine-tuning's to repair. s93a086adfc.summary: Researchers examine how to choose and fine-tune embodied foundation models for a fixed physical platform, splitting performance gaps into sensing and latency gaps.
s93a086adfc.why: Gives practitioners a framework for deciding whether benchmark-ranked robot checkpoints will work on their hardware before fine-tuning.

s0bfc5565bd.title: LSRP*-LA: Scalable and Anytime Multi-Agent Path Finding for Large Agents with Asynchronous Actions
s0bfc5565bd.description: arXiv:2611.33793v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) seeks collision-free paths for multiple agents from their start locations to their goal locations while minimizing path costs. Most MAPF algorithms assume that each agent occupies a single vertex and that the actions of all agents are synchronized. These assumptions may limit the use of MAPF planners in practice. Existing planners that get rid of both assumptions either handle only a few agents or cannot improve their solutions. Recently, a planner called LSRP* was proposed, which is scalable and anytime with asynchronous actions, but still limited by that each agent occupies a single vertex. s0bfc5565bd.summary: Researchers introduce LSRP*-LA, an anytime multi-agent path finding planner that handles large agents with asynchronous actions and scales to many agents.
s0bfc5565bd.why: Extends practical multi-robot path planning to larger agents and unsynchronized actions common in real warehouse or fleet settings.

sc05ac52cb0.title: QPAT: A Universal Quantum Machine Learning Framework for Quantum-Assisted Training and Classical Inference
sc05ac52cb0.description: arXiv:2611.33806v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep learning models often struggle with sharp local optima and overfitting in limited-data regimes, and exhibit limited capacity for capturing high-order, complex probability distributions. Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models, by operating in exponentially large Hilbert spaces, can efficiently represent such distributions and provide favorable inductive biases for learning, offering a promising pathway to overcome these limitations. However, their practical deployment in the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era is severely hindered by gradient coupling, barren plateaus, data-loading bottlenecks, and high inference latency. sc05ac52cb0.summary: Researchers propose QPAT, a quantum machine learning framework that uses quantum-assisted training while keeping classical inference.
sc05ac52cb0.why: Explores a hybrid path for NISQ hardware, though the text gives limited detail on practical gains.

sff19a7f47b.title: KnitNet: Learning to Search at Inference Time for Exact RNA Inverse Design
sff19a7f47b.description: arXiv:2611.33812v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: RNA inverse design seeks nucleotide sequences that fold into specified target structures. Existing methods rely on learned generators that can miss exact structural matches, especially beyond their training distributions, or on costly search over a vast, multimodal sequence space. Search is further complicated by globally coupled nucleotide interactions, as correcting one pairing error can create new errors beyond a fixed repair scope. To address this, we introduce KnitNet, an inference-time scaling framework that learns from verifier feedback to refine sequences for exact fold-back matching. Starting from candidates generated for a target secondary structure, KnitNet uses mismatched folds to infer nucleotide dependencies and adapt its join
sff19a7f47b.summary: Researchers introduce KnitNet, an inference-time search framework that uses verifier feedback to design RNA sequences that exactly fold into target structures.

s08075d3f42.title: FEAST: Fair and Efficient Adaptive Sampling for Task-Free On-Policy Learning
s08075d3f42.description: arXiv:2611.33827v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language agents trained from self-generated experience must allocate a limited rollout budget across heterogeneous capabilities. A common strategy is to prioritize capabilities with strong current learning signals, but in on-policy learning these signals are endogenous: past allocation changes the policy and therefore the evidence available for future allocation. This can create a feedback loop in which under-trained capabilities receive increasingly fewer opportunities to improve. We formalize this effect through the Quota-Efficiency Law (QEL), which shows that allocation history can change learning efficiency even under matched capability-specific exposure. s08075d3f42.summary: Researchers introduce FEAST, an adaptive sampling method for allocating limited rollout budgets across capabilities in task-free on-policy training of language agents.
s08075d3f42.why: Highlights a feedback loop where under-trained capabilities get fewer rollouts, relevant to teams training self-improving agents.

s6f7a1c27e0.title: When Rerankers Work Together: Better and Faster Reranking without Joint Training
s6f7a1c27e0.description: arXiv:2611.33844v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standalone reranker quality does not determine its value in a multistage RAG pipeline. We systematically study heterogeneous rerankers composed without joint training, spanning lexical, single-vector, late-interaction, and joint query-context scoring. Two lightweight semantic coarse scorers, Cache-Pointwise and Cache-Shapley, learn from passage relevance labels and share cacheable representations and linear-time singleton inference. Under matched candidates and budgets, we compare cascades with stage-removal references to measure evidence retention, repair and breakage, reader accuracy, and online pruning cost. s6f7a1c27e0.summary: Researchers study composing heterogeneous rerankers without joint training and propose lightweight coarse scorers that are both better and faster in multistage RAG pipelines.
s6f7a1c27e0.why: Offers practical guidance for improving retrieval quality and latency in RAG systems without costly retraining.

s89179b1d7f.title: Mitigating Overgeneralization in RND via Spectral Target Design
s89179b1d7f.description: arXiv:2611.33850v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Random Network Distillation (RND) is a scalable novelty signal for RL based on a fixed random target network and a trained predictor. However, it can overgeneralize: the predictor extrapolates the random target off the data manifold, causing novelty scores to collapse on unfamiliar inputs. s89179b1d7f.summary: Researchers analyze overgeneralization in Random Network Distillation for RL novelty detection and propose a spectral target design to mitigate it.
s89179b1d7f.why: Provides a kernel-based explanation and fix for novelty signals collapsing on unfamiliar inputs in RL exploration.

sfabd3a0e05.title: Random Voronoi Networks
sfabd3a0e05.description: arXiv:2611.33875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nearest-neighbor methods are local, simple, and interpretable, but their non-parametric form makes them memory-intensive, expensive at inference, and difficult to integrate into differentiable neural architectures. We introduce Random Voronoi Networks (RVNs), a family of structured three-layer MLPs that express nearest-neighbor geometry through sampled Voronoi comparisons. The first layer computes Random Voronoi Features (RVF) from affine pairwise separators between selected training samples, the second layer aggregates these comparisons into Voronoi cells or top-k neighborhood scores, and the readout layer produces classification or regression predictions. We show that, when all samples and pairwise comparisons are included, step RVNs reco
sfabd3a0e05.summary: Researchers introduce Random Voronoi Networks, structured three-layer MLPs that encode nearest-neighbor geometry via sampled Voronoi comparisons.
sfabd3a0e05.why: Offers a differentiable alternative to memory-heavy nearest-neighbor methods, though the text gives limited evaluation detail.

s659bc4ae46.title: When Are Parallel Subagents Effective for Coding? An Empirical Study on Repository Construction
s659bc4ae46.description: arXiv:2611.33893v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM-based coding agents are increasingly used for long-horizon tasks such as building an entire program from a specification. Products like Codex and Claude Code let an agent delegate work to parallel subagents, multiplying run cost, yet it remains unclear whether and when delegation produces a better program. We compare a single agent with a main agent delegating to subagents on repository-construction tasks from NL2Repo and ProgramBench (which also provides an executable reference program). We compare scores at equal time and equal cost, run intervention experiments, and analyze fine-grained behavior. s659bc4ae46.summary: An empirical study compares single coding agents with main agents delegating to parallel subagents on repository-construction tasks, at equal time and equal cost.
s659bc4ae46.why: Helps teams decide whether parallel subagent delegation justifies its multiplied run cost for long-horizon coding tasks.

s1381b50847.title: Correlation-Aware Evidential Fusion for Trusted Multi-View Classification
s1381b50847.description: arXiv:2611.33900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Trusted multi-view classification aims to make accurate and reliable predictions by integrating information from multiple views. Existing methods typically estimate class evidence and uncertainty for each view and combine the resulting opinions through aggregation rules. However, they generally treat different views as independent information sources, overlooking the correlations among them. Highly correlated views tend to produce similar evidence, and treating them as independent sources may repeatedly count consistent information and give it disproportionate influence, while weakening complementary evidence that provides additional information. Consequently, such correlation-unaware fusion may not only limit classification performance but
s1381b50847.summary: Researchers propose correlation-aware evidential fusion for trusted multi-view classification, accounting for correlated views that repeatedly count the same evidence.

s2f8de18b2d.title: DiCALM: Converting Autoregressive Convolution-Attention Language Models into Discrete Diffusion Language Models
s2f8de18b2d.description: arXiv:2611.33919v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing methods for adapting autoregressive (AR) language models to diffusion generation focus mainly on full-attention architectures. More efficient hybrid architectures remain underexplored. We introduce DiCALM, a recipe for converting the hybrid convolution-attention models of the LFM2 family (LFM2 and LFM2.5) from AR to masked-diffusion generation. s2f8de18b2d.summary: Researchers introduce DiCALM, a recipe for converting hybrid convolution-attention LFM2 language models from autoregressive to masked-diffusion text generation.
s2f8de18b2d.why: It shows a path to reuse existing hybrid AR models for diffusion generation rather than training diffusion models from scratch.

sf320574d45.title: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures
sf320574d45.description: arXiv:2611.33925v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robot world models are increasingly used to evaluate and plan policies, yet robot training data are dominated by successful demonstrations. Off the happy path, when a grasp is misaligned or mistimed and the object is pushed, tilted, or slips, their predictions break down. Across five pretrained action-conditioned models, object-motion error is at most 10.4% lower than that of a static baseline that copies the first frame, and two models are worse than this baseline. We present WorldReforge, which teaches world models what happens when manipulation goes wrong. We construct the Reforge dataset of 62k simulated trajectories by perturbing reference grasps in position, orientation, and closure timing, recording each resulting push, slip, or fail
sf320574d45.summary: WorldReforge is presented to teach robot world models how manipulation failures like misaligned grasps and slips unfold, after tested models underperformed a static baseline on failure cases.
sf320574d45.why: Robot world models used for policy evaluation and planning may be unreliable off the success path, which matters for deployment testing.

s4ac06d5874.title: Connecting AI Agents to Live Discrete Element Simulations via the Model Context Protocol
s4ac06d5874.description: arXiv:2611.33926v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper describes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server through which a general-purpose AI agent operates a discrete element engine, commercial or open-source, while the simulation runs. The human modeler stays at the engine's console and graphical interface throughout, and the agent sees what the modeler does there. s4ac06d5874.why: It demonstrates a concrete pattern for connecting agents to live engineering simulation tools through MCP.

s8a9cb79c80.title: Towards 360$^\circ$ Embodied UAV Tracking Without Turning
s8a9cb79c80.description: arXiv:2611.33934v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conventional embodied UAV tracking couples target observability with heading control because targets may leave the field of view of forward-facing cameras. We investigate a complementary paradigm that uses full-spherical perception to follow designated targets without active heading adjustment. To support this setting, we introduce 360UAV-ETrack, a simulation benchmark comprising 2,652 sequences, over 1.73 million synchronized observations, eight tracking tasks, and 150 held-out closed-loop scenarios. s8a9cb79c80.summary: Researchers introduce 360UAV-ETrack, a simulation benchmark of 2,652 sequences, and 360UAV-TVLA, a panoramic vision-based method for UAV tracking without turning to change heading.
s8a9cb79c80.why: Full-spherical perception could decouple target tracking from heading control for drones, a benchmark-level result rather than a deployed system.

sa0d2456a0b.title: InstructTTS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Objective Instruction-Following TTS
sa0d2456a0b.description: arXiv:2611.33937v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Instruction-following text-to-speech (Instruct-TTS) renders a target transcript in the manner described by a free-form natural-language instruction, and a good rendition must succeed on three fronts at once: following the instruction, pronouncing the transcript correctly, and sounding natural. Reinforcement learning has become the standard way to post-train such generative models toward human preferences, and TTS systems increasingly adopt it. When the three objectives are optimized together under a single scalar reward, typically with group relative policy optimization (GRPO), training tends to be unstable: the objectives compete, and the shared update drifts toward whichever one is easiest to improve, producing a seesaw among them. sa0d2456a0b.summary: InstructTTS-OPD proposes on-policy distillation to jointly optimize instruction following, pronunciation, and naturalness in instruction-following text-to-speech models.
sa0d2456a0b.why: It addresses the difficulty of balancing multiple objectives under a single scalar reward when post-training TTS models.

sc2117471d3.title: DuoMI: Dual Mutual Information Regularization for Expert Reuse in Looped Transformers
sc2117471d3.description: arXiv:2611.33952v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Dual Mutual Information Regularization (DuoMI), a method for regulating expert routing across rounds in looped mixture-of-experts (MoE) Transformers. sc2117471d3.summary: DuoMI introduces dual mutual information regularization to encourage expert reuse across rounds in looped mixture-of-experts Transformers.
sc2117471d3.why: Better expert routing across loop iterations could improve parameter efficiency in looped MoE architectures.

s93a0ea757b.title: RefMix: Expanding Endpoint Proposals for Diversity-Preserving Reward Fine-Tuning
s93a0ea757b.description: arXiv:2611.33957v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online forward matching aligns flow-based generative models by repeatedly generating, rewarding, and fitting model-produced endpoints. However, this behavior creates an on-policy feedback loop: as high-reward modes become increasingly favored, alternative modes become less likely to appear in subsequent training pools, progressively reducing visual diversity. s93a0ea757b.summary: RefMix proposes injecting reference-assisted alternative endpoint candidates into training pools to counter diversity loss in reward fine-tuning of flow-based generative models.
s93a0ea757b.why: It targets a feedback loop where reward fine-tuning progressively reduces visual diversity, relevant to training image generators.

s83407a526d.title: AI Buckingham: Agentic Discovery of Dimensionless Scaling Laws Across Physical Regimes
s83407a526d.description: arXiv:2611.33961v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classical dimensional analysis defines admissible dimensionless representations but does not determine which combinations capture the dominant physical dependence, whether it changes across physical regimes, or when dependent-variable rescaling is required. We present AI Buckingham, an agentic framework for autonomous dimensionless discovery from natural-language descriptions of physical problems and observational data. It couples reasoning and planning by a large language model (LLM) with predefined symbolic and numerical tools. s83407a526d.summary: AI Buckingham is an agentic framework pairing an LLM with symbolic and numerical tools to autonomously discover dimensionless scaling laws from problem descriptions and data.

s5fd96e20be.title: Embodied-VGGT: Preserving Reliable Local Geometry for Long-Sequence Reconstruction
s5fd96e20be.description: arXiv:2611.33964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long sequence reconstruction must correct accumulated drift while preserving locally consistent geometry. In robotics and autonomous driving, embodied acquisition provides recurring platform- environment geometry and repeated observations of scene structure and platform motion. We present Embodied-VGGT, which exploits these cues to establish reliable local relationships and selectively preserve them during global refinement. s5fd96e20be.summary: Embodied-VGGT is presented as a method for long-sequence 3D reconstruction that preserves reliable local geometry while correcting accumulated drift during global refinement.
s5fd96e20be.why: Drift correction in long-sequence reconstruction matters for robotics and autonomous driving mapping pipelines.

s7d741a4468.title: Fine-Tuning Without Gradients? Closed-Form, LLM-Written Classifiers on a Frozen Encoder
s7d741a4468.description: arXiv:2611.33972v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can a classifier computed in closed form on a frozen encoder match gradient fine-tuning? We present closed-form weight-space programming (WSP): a large language model (LLM), used as a design assistant, writes programs that read a frozen masked language model through cloze-style prompt templates at several layers, fit closed-form heads (shrinkage discriminant analysis, kernel ridge regression and the encoder's label-word prior) on labelled data, and select among a pool of candidate heads by cross-fitting. s7d741a4468.summary: Closed-form weight-space programming uses an LLM to write programs that fit closed-form classifier heads on a frozen masked language model, without gradient fine-tuning.
s7d741a4468.why: It suggests a gradient-free alternative to fine-tuning for classification, though the paper's results versus fine-tuning are not stated here.

sc8f1cffabc.title: Kolpona: An Agentic Framework with Gradient-Free Neuron Programming for RTL Generation
sc8f1cffabc.description: arXiv:2611.33973v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open-weight large language models (LLMs) for register-transfer level (RTL) design are usually improved by fine-tuning on curated Verilog corpora, which needs large sets of verified designs and GPU training. We present Kolpona, an agentic framework that improves such models without gradient training. sc8f1cffabc.summary: Kolpona is an agentic framework that improves open-weight LLMs for RTL Verilog generation via gradient-free neuron programming, keeping edits only when testbench results improve.
sc8f1cffabc.why: It offers a way to improve hardware-design LLMs without GPU fine-tuning or large verified Verilog corpora.

s7a5f963952.title: MolGPAO: Molecular Generative Pre-trained Autoregressive Octree with Speculative Decoding and Sub-Millisecond Seam Healing for 3D Molecules
s7a5f963952.description: arXiv:2611.33985v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autoregressive generation over adaptive 3D octrees (Uni-3DAR) offers an intrinsic $O(N \log N)$ sparsity advantage over dense $O(N^2)$ equivariant diffusion and flow models on large drug-like molecules, yet lags in geometric equilibrium, closed-shell valence stability, and property fidelity due to Morton-seam coordinate jumps, leaf-heavy compute with root-count trapping, and target-shortcut collapse in internal critics. s7a5f963952.summary: MolGPAO is a standalone 3D octree autoregressive architecture for molecule generation, adding speculative decoding and seam healing to address geometric and valence issues in prior methods.

sf6f11cf908.title: Aegis-VLA: Reliability-Gated Action Refinement via a Trajectory World Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation
sf6f11cf908.description: arXiv:2611.33993v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dynamic object manipulation requires maintaining spatial and temporal alignment with targets that continue to move during inference and execution. Although future prediction can inform action correction, an accurate forecast does not establish whether modifying an existing action would be beneficial. We present Aegis-VLA, a world-model-guided vision-language-action (VLA) framework that generates predictive action corrections and separately determines whether and how strongly to apply them. sf6f11cf908.summary: Aegis-VLA is a world-model-guided vision-language-action framework that generates predictive action corrections for dynamic object manipulation and decides whether to apply them.
sf6f11cf908.why: Gating corrections by reliability addresses a practical failure mode for robots manipulating moving objects.

sf8e9b4a90b.title: DosePET: An Open-Source Dataset with 2100 Radiation Dose Maps for PET/CT
sf8e9b4a90b.description: arXiv:2611.34008v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large collections of three-dimensional radiation dose maps linked to patient anatomy are needed to develop artificial intelligence (AI) models for personalized internal dosimetry in nuclear medicine, but access to such data remains limited. Here we present DosePET, an open-source dataset of 2,100 patient-specific absorbed-dose maps generated by Monte Carlo simulation of publicly available PET/CT examinations: 1,503 [18F]FDG examinations from ENHANCE.PET and 369 [18F]PSMA-1007 and 228 [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 examinations from PSMA-PET-CT-Lesions, acquired at five institutions with seven scanner models. sf8e9b4a90b.summary: DosePET is an open-source dataset of 2,100 Monte Carlo-simulated patient-specific absorbed-dose maps from publicly available PET/CT examinations.
sf8e9b4a90b.why: Public dose-map data could enable training AI models for personalized internal dosimetry in nuclear medicine.

s72f6324e3e.title: CARROT: Competitive Adaptive Graph Clustering via Semi-Relaxed Optimal Transport
s72f6324e3e.description: arXiv:2611.34012v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep graph clustering (DGC) has emerged as a prominent paradigm for unsupervised attributed graph clustering. However, existing methods often struggle with two practical challenges encountered in real-world applications: the number of clusters $K$ is unknown a priori, and cluster sizes are frequently highly imbalanced. Methods relying on a pre-specified $K$ may fail to recover the underlying clustering structure when $K$ is misspecified, while many approaches implicitly favor balanced partitions, hindering the discovery of minority clusters. s72f6324e3e.summary: CARROT is a deep graph clustering method using semi-relaxed optimal transport to handle unknown cluster counts and highly imbalanced cluster sizes.

s70c6cf8fda.title: Residual Cross-Model Narrative Convergence under Shared Prompts: Auditing Prompt Controls and Narrative Measurement
s70c6cf8fda.description: arXiv:2611.34015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stories created by LLMs based on the same prompts can be narratively similar to one another. This similarity may reflect constraints imposed by the prompts as well as the models' writing tendencies. The current research analyzes 51,240 stories created by five models in the StoryScope corpus based on 10,248 common prompts. It uses 213 narrative features in seven dimensions to compare cross-model distances between stories generated from the same prompts with distances between stories generated from different but semantically matched prompts.
