s70c6cf8fda.summary: Researchers analyze 51,240 LLM-generated stories from 10,248 shared prompts, comparing narrative similarity across five models using 213 features.
s70c6cf8fda.why: It helps teams separate prompt-driven narrative similarity from model-specific writing tendencies when evaluating or auditing generated content.

s2ec896930c.title: Evaluating Ukrainian Grammatical Competence in Language Models: Probability Versus Prompting
s2ec896930c.description: arXiv:2611.34016v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Organisations deploying large language models in Ukrainian-language information systems need to know whether a model produces normative Ukrainian. This paper establishes a protocol for measuring that reliably and applies it to 19 models. The instrument is a released set of 1,444 Ukrainian minimal pairs covering the vocative case, numeral-noun and adjective agreement, verb government and calques from russian, with subject-verb agreement as a control; a quarter of the set was checked against the answer key in two independent native-speaker ratings, which agreed at Cohen's $\kappa$ = 0.963. s2ec896930c.summary: Researchers released a set of 1,444 Ukrainian minimal pairs and used them to measure grammatical competence across 19 language models.
s2ec896930c.why: Organisations deploying LLMs in Ukrainian-language systems get a released benchmark and protocol for checking whether models produce normative Ukrainian.

s4b1b63c8be.title: Assessing the Physical Interpretability of AlphaEarth Foundation Embeddings Through Multi-Sensor Satellite Time-Series Benchmarking for Agricultural Mapping
s4b1b63c8be.description: arXiv:2611.34019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate and dynamic maps of agricultural LULC are important for agricultural water resource management, particularly in areas where water scarcity is prevalent, such as Morocco. Here, we evaluate the utility of AlphaEarth Foundation Model (AEF) embeddings for agricultural LULC and irrigation-type mapping in Morocco. AEF embeddings were compared to single-date and time-series remote-sensing features using three machine-learning classifiers: XGBoost, CatBoost, and TabPFN. s4b1b63c8be.summary: Researchers evaluated AlphaEarth Foundation embeddings for agricultural land-use and irrigation-type mapping in Morocco against multi-sensor satellite time-series features.
s4b1b63c8be.why: It offers evidence on whether pretrained geospatial embeddings can replace costlier time-series feature pipelines for agricultural mapping.

s0b92564eed.title: Incorporating the Knowledge Distillation to Improve the EfficientNet Transfer Learning Capability
s0b92564eed.description: arXiv:2611.34025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Due to the Deep Learning requirement for a large training dataset, Transfer Learning has become a central method in the field of Computer Vision, which heavily used Deep Learning. Since the adoption of transfer learning in the field, the performance of the models in computer vision is significantly upgraded. The common transfer learning practice in computer vision research is to use state-of-the-art architectures in the ImageNet dataset as the backbone network. The best performing architecture in ImageNet is currently held by EfficientNet, which is a set of architectures that were progressively grown from a baseline architecture. s0b92564eed.summary: The paper proposes incorporating knowledge distillation to improve transfer learning capability of EfficientNet models in computer vision.

s160e5aa878.title: Counter-DECEIVR: Counterfactual Explanations for Deepfake Detectors using Detector-Guided Rectified Flow Inversion
s160e5aa878.description: arXiv:2611.34032v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep-learning-generated media are increasingly passed off as real, driving an arms race between image generators and deepfake detectors. Trust in the latter is limited by their often black-box nature; and, while region-based explanations can sometimes be extracted, these become less useful as generation quality improves. Counterfactual examples, which show the minimal change that flips a detector's decision, reveal what evidence drives a verdict, helping analysts decide whether to trust it. s160e5aa878.summary: Researchers introduce Counter-DECEIVR, a method that generates counterfactual explanations for deepfake detectors using detector-guided rectified flow inversion.
s160e5aa878.why: Counterfactual explanations can show analysts which evidence drives a deepfake detector's verdict, helping them decide whether to trust it.

sdce7aa564f.title: Post-Training Policy Replication for Strategy-Following Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning across Team Sizes
sdce7aa564f.description: arXiv:2611.34035v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Although multi-agent deep reinforcement learning enables coordinated behavior, aligning it with managerial intent remains difficult due to complex agent interactions. Although the strategy-following distributed attentional actor architecture (sfDA7-X) improves controllability via regional instructions, instruction combinations scale exponentially with team and instruction sizes, leading to prohibitive training costs and poor transferability. sdce7aa564f.summary: Researchers propose a team-size-independent observation architecture and post-training policy replication for strategy-following multi-agent deep reinforcement learning.
sdce7aa564f.why: Reducing retraining costs when team sizes change could make managerially controlled multi-agent RL systems cheaper to scale and transfer.

s5b682dd5a1.title: Hijacking 3D Generation: Targeted Adversarial Attacks against Image-to-3D Models via Prefix Trajectory Alignment
s5b682dd5a1.description: arXiv:2611.34075v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online services that deploy Image-to-3D models enable users to generate high-quality 3D assets from a single image. However, the generated 3D geometry can violate content policies and cause broader security risks. To prevent such content, these services typically use policy-restricted inspectors to examine uploaded images before generation. Since the inspector examines only the visible content of the input, a visually benign image can still induce the generation of policy-restricted 3D geometry. s5b682dd5a1.why: Services relying on input-image inspectors for content policy may be bypassed, exposing generation pipelines to misuse and security risks.

safdc3f17fa.title: WorldBridge: Bridging Scattered Views for Coherent 3D World Generation
safdc3f17fa.description: arXiv:2611.34079v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generating coherent and explorable 3D worlds from scattered images with little or no visual overlap is a fundamental and long-standing challenge in computer vision, which existing geometry-aware methods fail to address. Meanwhile, existing image- and video-based methods may generate unseen regions but produce inconsistent geometry across views. safdc3f17fa.summary: WorldBridge is a framework for generating coherent, controllable 3D worlds from scattered images with little or no visual overlap.

s2e976358e4.title: Whose Side Are You On? A Framework and Benchmark for Assessing LLM Political Stances through Politicians Social Media Posts
s2e976358e4.description: arXiv:2611.34098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly participate in political discussions, making it important to understand which positions they support or oppose. s2e976358e4.summary: Researchers propose a framework and WorldPOLL benchmark of 4,600 politicians' X/Twitter posts to assess LLMs' political stances through simulated social media interactions.
s2e976358e4.why: Teams deploying LLMs in political or public-facing contexts can use this framework to measure which stances models consistently express.

s4cc6b1e1c3.title: Will AI Replace Juniors? How Task Complexity Reduces Automation Risk
s4cc6b1e1c3.description: arXiv:2611.34099v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How does task complexity shape firms' willingness to substitute entry-level labour with artificial intelligence (AI) tools? We study this question using a pre-registered survey experiment with managers from 1,435 German firms in the information economy and manufacturing industry. Managers are randomly assigned to consider a long lasting need for additional capacity involving either well-structured and standardised tasks, or more complex tasks that require professional judgement, contextual knowledge and independent problem-solving. s4cc6b1e1c3.summary: A pre-registered survey experiment with managers from 1,435 German firms examines how task complexity affects willingness to replace entry-level labour with AI.
s4cc6b1e1c3.why: Leaders planning junior hiring may find that managers view complex, judgement-heavy tasks as less exposed to AI substitution than standardised ones.

s966c69652e.title: AlignPre: Skill-Aligned Post-Training for Latent-Free Generative Precipitation Nowcasting
s966c69652e.description: arXiv:2611.34101v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Precipitation nowcasting requires accurate short-term predictions under rapidly evolving spatiotemporal dynamics. Generative diffusion models can produce detailed and competitive radar forecasts by modeling conditional distributions. s966c69652e.summary: AlignPre is a pixel-space generative diffusion framework for precipitation nowcasting that aligns post-training with operational forecast skill, without latent compression modules.

s212095d9ab.title: Do Machine Learning Ensembles Beat Published Quotas? Target Parameterization, Censored Baselines, and Conformal Intervals Under Admissions Reform
s212095d9ab.description: arXiv:2611.34104v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Public admission capacity caps published prior to matriculation are widely used by ministries and institutional analysts as default intake projections in centralized postsecondary clearinghouses. sdb71e8a03f.title: SysBio-SR: Benchmarking Symbolic Regression for Trajectory Fidelity and Mechanism Recovery in Systems Biology
sdb71e8a03f.description: arXiv:2611.34106v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symbolic regression seeks to discover interpretable governing equations for dynamical systems from data. sdb71e8a03f.summary: Researchers introduce SysBio-SR, a benchmark of 198 literature-based biological ODE systems to test whether symbolic regression recovers true reaction mechanisms.
sdb71e8a03f.why: Shows that accurate trajectory fitting does not guarantee recovery of underlying mechanisms, so evaluation of scientific model-discovery tools needs mechanism-level checks.

s8fdf8b417c.title: Unstable Action Boundaries in Lethal Drone Agents
s8fdf8b417c.description: arXiv:2611.34121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents raise safety risks that are not captured by text-only refusal behavior, especially when tools can trigger high-impact actions. s8fdf8b417c.summary: A study tests whether tool-using LLM drone agents keep stable action boundaries when target descriptors change in a simulated perception-action pipeline over drone imagery.
s8fdf8b417c.why: Tool-using agents that can trigger high-impact actions may behave unpredictably under small input changes, a safety concern beyond text-only refusal behavior.

sd2a395e74c.title: MUSE: Multi-Task Uncertainty-Aware Self-Supervised Encoder for mmWave ISAC
sd2a395e74c.description: arXiv:2611.34122v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) allows a wireless system to use the same waveform for communication and environment sensing. At mmWave frequency bands, ISAC enables diverse human sensing tasks, such as localization, gesture recognition, and pose estimation, with high precision. sd2a395e74c.summary: MUSE is a multi-task, uncertainty-aware self-supervised encoder for mmWave integrated sensing and communication that aims to support multiple sensing tasks from one model.
sd2a395e74c.why: A shared encoder with uncertainty estimates could reduce per-task training and flag unreliable predictions in mmWave sensing systems.

s842738ac4a.title: Out of Sight, Not Out of Clues: Can Video LLMs Guess from Partial Evidence?
s842738ac4a.description: arXiv:2611.34126v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In real-world applications like egocentric recording, visual accessibility, and surveillance review, visual evidence for Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) is often only partially captured. A reliable model should match its response to the evidence: answering when sufficient, guessing from visible clues when partial, and abstaining when absent. s842738ac4a.summary: Researchers argue existing Video LLM benchmarks use a binary answerable-or-unanswerable split, leaving partial visual evidence unmeasured, and propose evaluating responses to partial evidence.
s842738ac4a.why: Engineers deploying video models in surveillance or accessibility need to know whether models answer, guess, or abstain appropriately when evidence is incomplete.

s6f950bb8f5.title: FoundSurface: Feedforward Ray-Based 3D Scene Surface Reconstruction from Unposed Images
s6f950bb8f5.description: arXiv:2611.34128v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate 3D surface reconstruction from unposed images remains a fundamental challenge in computer vision. s6f950bb8f5.why: It offers a camera-pose-free route to dense 3D surfaces, which could simplify reconstruction pipelines for vision and robotics teams.

s7e523f9148.title: WorldPhy: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Physical Plausibility of World Models in Robotics
s7e523f9148.description: arXiv:2611.34130v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World models are increasingly used in robotics to improve the performance of embodied models. Compared with general-purpose video generation, robotics places more stringent requirements on world models. Generated videos must satisfy fine-grained physical constraints on robot motion and object interactions. However, existing world model benchmarks can overlook robotics specific physical details and struggle to assess them accurately. s7e523f9148.summary: WorldPhy is a new benchmark for evaluating fine-grained physical plausibility of robotics world models, covering robot motion and object interactions.
s7e523f9148.why: Teams using generated video as world models for robots need finer physics checks than general video-generation benchmarks provide.

s3ce0178dc0.title: Reproducer Synthesis for AI-Reported Bugs in the Linux Kernel
s3ce0178dc0.description: arXiv:2611.34142v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic review systems are increasingly flagging suspected bugs in Linux kernel patches as textual reports. A maintainer who receives such reports needs further inspection to determine whether the report is true. The inspection requires understanding whether the bug can be triggered and, if necessary, manually constructing one. As a consequence, despite the excessive textual explanation, many reports go unanswered. In this paper, we argue that a runnable proof-of-concept (PoC) is the key information in such AI-generated kernel review reports. s3ce0178dc0.summary: The paper argues that runnable proof-of-concept reproducers should accompany AI-generated bug reports for Linux kernel patches, to help maintainers verify them.
s3ce0178dc0.why: Maintainers and kernel teams receiving AI review reports could triage faster if each report included a runnable reproducer.

s2715a7dd12.title: Lost in the Grid: Where Multimodal LLMs Fail Between Seeing and Planning
s2715a7dd12.description: arXiv:2611.34152v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) excel at static visual understanding and are increasingly applied to spatial planning, where a model interprets a visual layout and outputs an action sequence to reach a goal. Grid games are a common testbed for this ability because their rules are explicit and a solver can verify every move. Yet existing benchmarks mostly report end-to-end success rates, which hide whether a failure stems from visual perception, rule application, or multi-step planning. s2715a7dd12.summary: GridProbe is a diagnostic benchmark that separates visual perception, rule application, and multi-step planning failures in multimodal LLMs on grid games.
s2715a7dd12.why: End-to-end success rates hide where spatial planning fails, so this benchmark helps engineers locate the actual weakness in MLLM agents.

s769b512614.title: Strategic and Robust Task Allocation for Combat Objectives in Adversarial Multi-Agent Environments
s769b512614.description: arXiv:2611.34158v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Task allocation in contested-objective team games requires coordinated decisions under uncertainty, spatial constraints, and changing tactical conditions. In such settings, multiple agents must anticipate both teammate behavior and opponent actions. We study a hybrid predict-then-optimize approach for assigning controllable agents to objectives in real time. A masked multi-head model predicts tactical signals for each agent, including survival chance, local superiority, combat interaction, travel time, and objective contribution. These signals are combined with rule-based terms in a score matrix, and a minimum-cost flow solver computes coordinated global assignments constrained by capacity, occupancy, stability, and defensive strategies. s769b512614.summary: Researchers propose a hybrid predict-then-optimize method that uses a masked multi-head model to assign agents to objectives in adversarial team games in real time.
s769b512614.why: The approach combines tactical prediction with optimization for multi-agent allocation under uncertainty, relevant to teams building coordinated agent systems.

sdc5dcf42f1.title: Multi-view fnirs identifies neurophysiological subtypes in post-stroke aphasia
sdc5dcf42f1.description: arXiv:2611.34169v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-stroke aphasia is clinically heterogeneous, and conventional classifications may not capture differences in brain functional organisation. sdc5dcf42f1.summary: A study of 79 post-stroke aphasia patients used multi-view fNIRS and unsupervised clustering to identify neurophysiological subtypes.

s36be01f6b8.title: Agentic-Level Adversarial Purification: Revisiting Diffusion Purifiers on Native-Resolution Agentic Inputs
s36be01f6b8.description: arXiv:2611.34181v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language agents act on native-resolution renders of multi-element pages, where one perturbed photo or a few altered text strokes can redirect the decision. Any content provider can craft such a perturbation on the open model behind the agent, so a plug-in purifier is the natural first line of defense. Yet diffusion purifiers were designed and evaluated at the fixed resolution of the diffusion model on classifier or natural-image benchmarks, and defense evaluations for agents test JPEG, blur and noise but no diffusion purifier. s36be01f6b8.summary: The paper revisits diffusion purifiers as defenses for vision-language agents on native-resolution inputs, which prior agent defense evaluations did not test.
s36be01f6b8.why: Engineers securing vision-language agents against adversarial page perturbations get an evaluation of a plug-in purifier defense they may adopt.

s3fafb53ab9.title: Hierarchical Semantic Learning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Missing Modalities
s3fafb53ab9.description: arXiv:2611.34184v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) in real-world systems must handle unpredictable modality missingness caused by sensor failures, privacy masking, and unstable transmission. Existing methods either learn reliability-aware representations or reconstruct missing inputs, often using a single flattened encoder output. This overlooks deep encoders' semantic hierarchy and intra- and inter-modal interactions, causing semantic averaging and ill-posed mappings. s3fafb53ab9.summary: Hierarchical Semantic Learning (HSL) is proposed for multimodal sentiment analysis, handling missing modalities by exploiting semantic hierarchy in deep encoders.
s3fafb53ab9.why: Robust handling of missing sensor or input modalities matters for real-world multimodal systems with unreliable transmission.

se302a6283f.title: MINE: A Training-Free Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection via Mutual Information and Embedding Variance
se302a6283f.description: arXiv:2611.34188v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing defenses against indirect prompt injection in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) are inherently reactive: prompt-engineering methods are often overridden by the injected instructions, while supervised detectors must be retrained for each new attack style. se302a6283f.summary: MINE is a training-free defense against indirect prompt injection in RAG that maximizes relevance via mutual information and embedding variance, and also works as a reranker.
se302a6283f.why: It offers an attack-agnostic defense that needs no retraining, which is useful for teams running retrieval-augmented systems exposed to injected content.

s0d5f752ef4.title: Beyond Logits: Coherent Hallucination Mitigation via Attention Contrastive Decoding
s0d5f752ef4.description: arXiv:2611.34207v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) demonstrate impressive multimodal capabilities, yet suffer from hallucination - generating factually inaccurate content. Contrastive Decoding (CD) mitigates this by contrasting amateur and expert branches at the logit level. s0d5f752ef4.summary: Attention Contrastive Decoding (ACD) is a training-free plug-in that reduces hallucination in vision-language models by contrasting attention rather than logits.
s0d5f752ef4.why: It targets hallucination mitigation without degrading generation coherence, a tradeoff that affects deployed LVLM output quality.

s646d942d9e.title: GeoCAM: Self-Supervised Sonar-Optical Representation Learning via Geographic Overlap Supervision
s646d942d9e.description: arXiv:2611.34218v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cross-modal self-supervised learning for paired side-scan sonar and underwater optical imagery is a promising direction for benthic habitat understanding, but it remains underexplored because existing methods do not fully exploit the one-to-many correspondences and geographic metadata available in real opti-acoustic surveys. This limits the ability to learn representations that are both semantically meaningful and geometrically consistent from abundant unlabeled marine data. s646d942d9e.summary: GeoCAM is a geography-guided self-supervised framework that learns representations linking side-scan sonar and underwater optical imagery for benthic habitat understanding.

s66c1d99a84.title: The Socratic PAUSE: safeguarding scientific judgement at AI speed
s66c1d99a84.description: arXiv:2611.34222v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI can turn a tentative scientific question into hypotheses, methods, code and interpretations within minutes. Yet generating a contribution does not establish that it deserves scientific reliance: researchers must still examine its evidence, assumptions and implications, and remain accountable for the decision to rely on it. Using Einstein's sketch of scientific discovery as a lens, we argue that AI has accelerated discovery far more than justification. In human-AI research partnerships, confidence can therefore outgrow evidence through three mechanisms: recursive reinforcement, loss of provenance and miscalibrated reliance on AI-generated contributions. s66c1d99a84.summary: The paper argues AI has accelerated scientific discovery far more than justification, and proposes safeguards so researchers evaluate AI-generated evidence before relying on it.
s66c1d99a84.why: Research teams adopting generative AI for hypotheses and code need checks that keep confidence tied to evidence.

saf4a833523.title: Weakly Conditioned Diffusion Model Augmentation for Prostate Segmentation
saf4a833523.description: arXiv:2611.34230v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep learning models for prostate MRI segmentation often struggle to generalize when trained on limited heterogeneous data, leading to boundary errors and over-segmentation. We present an augmentation framework using mask-conditioned synthetic and diverse T2-weighted MRI volumes to improve boundary precision and reduce over-segmentation. We employ a 2.5D weakly mask-conditioned denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) via channel concatenation. saf4a833523.summary: A 2.5D mask-conditioned diffusion model generates synthetic T2-weighted prostate MRI volumes to augment training data for segmentation.
saf4a833523.why: Synthetic conditioned augmentation can reduce boundary errors and over-segmentation when medical training data is limited and heterogeneous.

sc995508d63.title: LLM-coupled interpretable tool wear monitoring with multi-evidence reasoning in CNC machining
sc995508d63.description: arXiv:2611.34270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Interpretable tool wear assessment in CNC machining is challenging. Existing diagnostic models have high accuracy but provide limited guidance for tool replacement. This study proposes a two layer framework combining deep learning wear classification and LLM assisted reasoning. The first layer uses PCA Loading feature selection and optimized GRU to recognize three wear states, achieving 98.38 percent macro F1 score on the PHM2010 dataset. The second layer uses LLMs to generate natural language reports and replacement suggestions from classification results and feature trends. Engineer evaluation shows the reports outperform rule templates. Cross dataset tests on NASA milling data support the generalizability of this framework.
sc995508d63.summary: A two-layer framework combines a GRU wear classifier, reporting 98.38% macro F1 on PHM2010, with LLM-generated reports and replacement suggestions for CNC tool wear.
sc995508d63.why: It shows pairing a classifier with LLM reasoning to produce interpretable maintenance guidance for industrial monitoring systems.

s5fbd1e925c.title: LatentCP-DPO: Conformal Pessimism for DPO with Finite-Sample Guarantees
s5fbd1e925c.description: arXiv:2611.34275v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) learns a response policy from human preference data, but with a limited dataset it can overfit to noisy or weakly informative preference labels. s5fbd1e925c.why: Offers a finite-sample-guaranteed way to make preference tuning more robust when labeled preference data is scarce or noisy.

sb0c8f3c93e.title: Latent-in-the-Middle: On the Security of Cross-Model Latent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
sb0c8f3c93e.description: arXiv:2611.34278v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As large language models increasingly collaborate in heterogeneous multi-agent systems, latent communication has emerged as an efficient alternative to exchanging natural-language messages. By sharing internal representations, agents can avoid repeatedly processing the same context, reducing communication overhead and prefill computation. One such mechanism is cross-model Key-Value (KV) cache transfer, which uses a learned mapper to translate a source model's KV cache into one a target model can use. sb0c8f3c93e.summary: A paper examines the security of cross-model latent communication, where a learned mapper translates one LLM's KV cache for use by another in multi-agent systems.
sb0c8f3c93e.why: Shared internal representations between agents may open security risks that natural-language messaging does not, which matters for multi-agent system design.

sb9a6b5b383.title: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation
sb9a6b5b383.description: arXiv:2611.34290v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern video foundation models generate high-quality short clips, but preserving long-video consistency and correctly depicting event-driven state changes remain challenging. Existing agentic workflows face these challenges because continual planning and repair accumulate context, while reference updates remain limited. We introduce StateWeaver, which combines Active States and Hierarchical Collaboration to connect review-driven visual reference updates with cross-shot state inheritance. sb9a6b5b383.why: Shows how agentic planning and review loops can address long-horizon consistency limits of current video foundation models.

sa64f26372e.title: WebVibe: Multimodal Interactive Website Generation via Reverse Synthesis and Visual Self-Distillation
sa64f26372e.description: arXiv:2611.34292v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Although multimodal large language models translate single screenshots into static HTML, generating interactive functional websites from design specifications still struggles with multi-page routing and stateful widget transitions. sa64f26372e.why: Targets known weaknesses in generating stateful, multi-page web apps from multimodal models, relevant to automated front-end tooling.

s3bc058e630.title: RAP: Radial-Angular Random Projection for Hyperbolic Representations
s3bc058e630.description: arXiv:2611.34298v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Random projection is a basic compression primitive for Euclidean representation learning, with the Johnson--Lindenstrauss lemma giving a target dimension $k=O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log n)$ independent of the ambient dimension. s3bc058e630.why: Provides a dimensionality reduction tool for hyperbolic embeddings used in some Transformers and vision-language models.

s935bc19f42.title: The cost of being seen as AI in group bargaining
s935bc19f42.description: arXiv:2611.34322v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded in collective decision-making, people's perceptions of AI may shape who reaches agreement and what they receive. s935bc19f42.summary: A study of 2,234 participants in a repeated three-player bargaining game finds players presented as AI received fewer points and were included in fewer final agreements.
s935bc19f42.why: Suggests labeling systems as AI may carry social costs in group decisions, relevant to deploying AI agents in negotiation settings.

sccadd24df6.title: LUDIUS: A Benchmark for Embodied Social Intelligence in Everyday Human-Robot Interactions
sccadd24df6.description: arXiv:2611.34328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Social intelligence in a robot requires interpreting a situation from the perspectives of the people involved and using that understanding to decide when and how to act. sccadd24df6.summary: LUDIUS is a benchmark evaluating vision-language models on embodied social intelligence across 15 skills in everyday human-robot interactions.
sccadd24df6.why: Gives teams a structured way to assess social judgment of VLM-driven robots beyond task success.

s2d0482c46c.title: Puzzling-Bench: Evaluating Language Models on 23,777 Human-Written Puzzles with Community-Verified Answers
s2d0482c46c.description: arXiv:2611.34331v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Puzzling-Bench, a benchmark of 23,777 puzzles with community-verified answers drawn from the Puzzling Stack Exchange archive (2014-2026): riddles, ciphers, logic grids, lateral-thinking problems, wordplay and recreational mathematics, a third of them with images. s2d0482c46c.summary: Puzzling-Bench introduces a benchmark of 23,777 community-verified puzzles from Puzzling Stack Exchange, including riddles, ciphers, logic grids, and images.

se864fbff8b.title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning with State-Dependent Foresight for Human Decision-Making
se864fbff8b.description: arXiv:2611.34351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computational modeling of behavior represents individuals with a model fitted to their observed behavior and characterizes them through its parameters. Naturalistic tasks incorporate the complexity of real environments and yield high-dimensional behavioral trajectories. se864fbff8b.why: Offers a modeling approach that better fits real human planning horizons, though the text gives little on practical applications.

s1a8125be1e.title: ConTra: A Training Framework for Effective Contextual Retrieval via Prefix Generation
s1a8125be1e.description: arXiv:2611.34366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data management systems organize large text collections for tasks such as finding relevant studies and extracting contract clauses. s1a8125be1e.summary: ConTra is a training framework that improves contextual retrieval by generating text prefixes that keep chunks searchable while preserving document context.
s1a8125be1e.why: Addresses a common RAG problem where chunking strips identifying context, relevant to retrieval pipeline design.

sd1b25a9b29.title: When Skills Fail to Compose: Compatibility and Retention in Language Models
sd1b25a9b29.description: arXiv:2611.34398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Skill acquisition alone does not establish a reusable skill library: task proficiency does not specify a compositional interface. sb27a123d8b.title: SemProxy: Semantic 3D Proxies for Controllable Agentic 3D Modeling
sb27a123d8b.description: arXiv:2611.34414v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents are increasingly capable of generating 3D models, yet enabling users to effectively control the modeling process remains challenging. s608733b47e.title: CHASE: Curiosity-Guided Skill Acquisition for Embodied Task Execution
s608733b47e.description: arXiv:2611.34416v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robots executing tasks in partially observed environments must resolve uncertainty while operating with incomplete skills. se00ebe4c27.title: Calibration of Neuromusculoskeletal Models Using Differentiable Physics: Recommendations for Improving Model Accuracy
se00ebe4c27.description: arXiv:2611.34428v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Differentiable physics has shown potential to usher in a new paradigm in human neuromusculoskeletal (NMS) model calibration. s186414e1fe.title: One Representation to Rule Them All -- Open-Vocabulary Change Detection from Text or Visual Examples
s186414e1fe.description: arXiv:2611.34430v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open-vocabulary change detection (OVCD) aims to localise user-specified changes without retraining for predefined categories. s741fe5fe41.title: Most of the Way There: Turning a Strong Video Prior into an Action-Conditioned World Model
s741fe5fe41.description: arXiv:2611.34435v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern video generators excel at producing visually plausible futures guided by text and image prompts. Yet their emphasis on semantic plausibility does not guarantee fidelity to the physical consequences of specific actions. Action-conditioned world models (ACWMs), in contrast, aim to simulate how the world responds to robot actions, enabling scalable policy evaluation and improvement without costly real-world rollouts. The challenge is not merely to generate a plausible future, but to predict what follows from a specific physical action. As video priors grow stronger, we ask how little adaptation is truly needed to bridge this gap. s741fe5fe41.summary: Researchers describe turning a strong video generation prior into an action-conditioned world model that simulates how the world responds to specific robot actions.
s741fe5fe41.why: It offers a path to scalable robot policy evaluation and improvement without costly real-world rollouts, though the excerpt gives limited detail on results.

s335348c4a4.title: ProxyGenBench: Benchmarking Proxy-Guided Video Generation
s335348c4a4.description: arXiv:2611.34457v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent video generators produce realistic videos, yet controlling how scenes unfold remains challenging. Structural proxies, such as animated 3D blockouts, guide generation by specifying scene layout, motion, camera behavior, and event order. However, these coarse inputs leave details unspecified and may contain artifacts that should not be reproduced. Successful proxy-guided generation must therefore Preserve intended structure, Complete missing content and correct proxy artifacts, and Bind text, image, and audio conditions to the right entities and events. s335348c4a4.summary: Researchers introduce ProxyGenBench, a benchmark for video generation guided by structural proxies such as animated 3D blockouts.
s335348c4a4.why: It gives teams a standard way to test whether generators preserve layout and motion intent while fixing proxy artifacts and binding text, image, and audio conditions.

sfdb0942993.title: Noise threshold for learning with quantum memory
sfdb0942993.description: arXiv:2611.34474v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A quantum memory can reduce exponentially the number of experiments needed to learn a physical process, but real memories are noisy. Here we show that, for Pauli memory noise with eigenvalues $\lambda_X,\lambda_Y,\lambda_Z$, the advantage is governed by $\lambda_X^2+\lambda_Y^2+\lambda_Z^2$. We prove that no protocol with an entangled probe gains an exponential advantage when this sum is at most one, reduce the general case to the additivity of a R\'enyi-2 coherent information, and find coded memories that retain a growing advantage within 1% of this threshold. sfdb0942993.summary: A paper shows that for Pauli memory noise, quantum memory's learning advantage depends on a sum of squared eigenvalues, with a noise threshold for exponential gains.
sfdb0942993.why: It clarifies noise limits for quantum learning hardware, though its direct relevance to most engineering teams is limited.

sb4c7e9e8c5.title: Angular Interpolation in Sparse-View Low-Dose CT Reconstruction: Placement Effects and Data-Consistency Step-Size Scaling
sb4c7e9e8c5.description: arXiv:2611.34508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dual-domain networks combine projection and image processing for sparse-view low-dose computed tomography (CT). We quantify the contribution of angular interpolation before learning and distinguish its roles in sinogram initialisation and the image residual base. On synthetic parallel-beam data, parameter-free interpolation reduces noise-free missing-view mean absolute error by 99.7% relative to zero filling at 60 views. Full-view filtered back-projection (FBP) of the jointly learned completed sinogram adds 1.27 dB of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) over interpolated FBP. In a data-consistency dual-domain network (DC-DuNet), a 2x2 configuration ablation controls branch width, depth and training schedule while varying these placements and
sb4c7e9e8c5.summary: A study on sparse-view low-dose CT reconstruction examines how angular interpolation placement and data-consistency step sizes affect dual-domain network performance.
sb4c7e9e8c5.why: It offers practical guidance for preprocessing choices in medical imaging reconstruction pipelines, based on synthetic parallel-beam data.

s3dcc35405b.title: Long-Horizon Planning with Latent World Models via Graph Anchors
s3dcc35405b.description: arXiv:2611.34509v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Latent world models plan in a compact latent space by predicting the outcomes of actions. Their planners judge a plan by the latent distance between its predicted end state and the goal image. We show that this distance fails in two distinct ways. First, it loses directional signal a few steps from the goal, causing distant goals to fail. Second, it weighs the robot arm over the manipulated object, causing manipulation to fail at contact. We measure both failures directly on recorded data by asking whether a lower latent distance corresponds to true progress toward the goal. Across five environments, six visual representations (including raw pixels and V-JEPA 2), and nine Meta-World tasks, this ranking test cleanly separates the two failure
s3dcc35405b.summary: Researchers propose graph anchors to improve long-horizon planning with latent world models, addressing failures of latent distance as a planning metric.
s3dcc35405b.why: It identifies specific failure modes of latent-distance planners in robotics, which matter for teams building model-based manipulation systems.

s5b000b15ae.title: PURA: Video Token Pruning via Unified Spatiotemporal Redundancy Assessment
s5b000b15ae.description: arXiv:2611.34521v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video large language models incur substantial inference costs from long visual token sequences. Existing video token compression methods mitigate these costs by exploiting spatial redundancy within frames and temporal redundancy across frames. However, many approaches impose predefined processing orders or fixed allocation ratios for spatial and temporal compression, limiting their ability to adapt to the varying balance of spatiotemporal redundancy across videos. To address this limitation, we propose PURA, a training-free method that prunes visual tokens through unified spatiotemporal redundancy assessment. For each token, PURA constructs spatial and temporal reference candidates and selects the reference with the lowest representation er
s5b000b15ae.summary: PURA is a training-free method that prunes video tokens by jointly assessing spatial and temporal redundancy in video large language models.
s5b000b15ae.why: Reducing long visual token sequences without retraining can lower inference costs for video LLM deployments.

sb84b98fb6f.title: EPPC-CARE: Staged Hierarchical Annotation of Communication Behaviors in Secure Patient-Provider Messages
sb84b98fb6f.description: arXiv:2611.34539v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Objectives: Patient portal messages provide invaluable information about communication dynamics between patients and healthcare providers, but extracting it manually is labor-intensive. We developed and evaluated EPPC-CARE, an automated framework for identifying communication behaviors together with the supporting text for each classification. Materials and Methods: From 867 messages, we obtained 5,516 reference standard annotations. Each annotation is a triplet of communication-related text (span), a broader communication category (Code), and a specific subcategory (Sub-code). We evaluated EPPC-CARE's identified triplets across six open-weight large language models (LLMs) against supervised fine-tuning and communication-based models such a
sb84b98fb6f.summary: EPPC-CARE is an automated framework for annotating communication behaviors in secure patient-provider portal messages, evaluated on 867 messages.
sb84b98fb6f.why: It shows how automated annotation can reduce manual labor in analyzing clinical messaging, relevant to health-tech builders.

s4425bb71eb.title: HAS: Hierarchical Adaptive Frame Sampling for Video Understanding
s4425bb71eb.description: arXiv:2611.34544v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Due to context-length constraints, most MLLMs cannot process full-length videos and therefore rely on sampling a subset of frames as input. However, existing sampling methods, ranging from uniform sampling to relevance-based selection, are often driven by a single sampling principle and thus struggle to accommodate the heterogeneous evidential requirements of different queries: some demand a holistic understanding of how the video unfolds over time, while others hinge on fine-grained events within a short temporal window. To address this limitation, we propose \textbf{Hierarchical Adaptive Frame Sampling (HAS)}, a two-stage frame sampling framework. s4425bb71eb.summary: HAS is a hierarchical adaptive frame sampling method that helps multimodal LLMs choose video frames for queries needing either holistic or fine-grained understanding.
s4425bb71eb.why: Better frame selection can improve video understanding accuracy within fixed context-length limits.

se09b8ca673.title: Recalling the Past to Answer the Present: Context-Aware Multi-Evidence Reasoning for Streaming Video Question Answering
se09b8ca673.description: arXiv:2611.34545v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in video understanding, yet existing video question answering (VQA) benchmarks mainly evaluate models in offline settings. Real-world streaming scenarios instead require models to answer context-dependent queries by retrieving and reasoning over evidence distributed across the video history. We introduce StreamRecall, a benchmark for context-aware Multi evidence reasoning in streaming video QA. StreamRecall requires models to retrieve, associate, and reason over temporally scattered evidence to answer queries at the appropriate moment. It contains 4,983 questions over 462 videos, with context-aligned query times and fine-grained temporal evidence annotations. We further propose
se09b8ca673.summary: StreamRecall is a benchmark testing vision-language models on answering context-dependent questions over temporally scattered evidence in streaming video.
se09b8ca673.why: It exposes limits of current offline-evaluated video QA models in real-time streaming scenarios that product teams may target.

se07a38b9a6.title: An Information-Theoretic Analysis of Information Hiding in Semantic Communication
se07a38b9a6.description: arXiv:2611.34550v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Semantic communication shifts the transmission goal from the accurate recovery of syntactic symbols to the reliable conveyance of semantic content, yet a systematic information-theoretic characterization of information hiding at the semantic layer is still missing. Building on the semantic information theory of Niu-Zhang and the classical information hiding theory of Moulin-O'Sullivan, this paper establishes an information-theoretic framework for information hiding under semantic communication. se07a38b9a6.summary: The paper develops an information-theoretic framework for information hiding within semantic communication, extending classical hiding models to a semantic layer.
se07a38b9a6.why: The text gives little on practical implications; it is primarily theoretical work on semantic communication security.

s09d9e4445e.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
s09d9e4445e.description: arXiv:2611.34575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Establishing effective scaling laws for medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains a persistent and fundamental challenge. Our systematic evaluation shows that existing medical MLLMs tend to underperform frontier general-purpose MLLMs across a range of medical tasks, while scaling model size primarily improves text capabilities rather than multimodal perception, and enabling reasoning modes fails to close this visual gap. To investigate how medical multimodal intelligence scales in practice, we introduce Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter medical multimodal model with 3B activated parameters, built by combining stage-specific curation over 322.7 million candidate records with a progressive training curriculum spanning medical p
s09d9e4445e.summary: Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter medical multimodal model, is introduced alongside findings that scaling mainly improves text rather than visual capabilities.
s09d9e4445e.why: The finding that medical MLLMs trail general models on visual tasks and scaling doesn't fix this is useful for healthcare AI planning.

s53d046c3df.title: Tune for Retention, Not Just Gain: SFT Forgets Far Less than You Think
s53d046c3df.description: arXiv:2611.34579v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Catastrophic forgetting, the drastic loss of previously acquired capabilities when learning new ones, is a central challenge in language model fine-tuning. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is widely believed to be prone to such forgetting. Recent works have attributed this to the off-policy nature of SFT, arguing that on-policy learning is key to continual learning. In this paper, we challenge this premise. s53d046c3df.summary: The paper argues that supervised fine-tuning forgets far less than assumed when hyperparameters such as lower learning rates are chosen for retention.
s53d046c3df.why: Teams fine-tuning LLMs can reduce catastrophic forgetting through hyperparameter choices rather than switching to on-policy methods.

s3f48f913d3.title: VisualMontage: Manipulating the Beliefs of Vision-Language Agents with Authentic Image Sequences
s3f48f913d3.description: arXiv:2611.34603v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As agents based on vision-language models (VLMs) increasingly interpret social-media content, errors in their analysis may lend credibility to rumors and amplify their spread. In this paper, we study the problem of visual cognitive collusion, in which coordinated posts combine authentic images and locally faithful captions to induce VLM agents to infer and accept attacker-chosen target claims through their own reasoning. To enable systematic evaluation of this cognitive threat, we introduce a new benchmark comprising 544 target cases and 33.2K candidate images across eight application domains. s3f48f913d3.summary: VisualMontage introduces a benchmark of 544 target cases showing how coordinated posts with authentic images and faithful captions can steer vision-language agents toward attacker-chosen claims.
s3f48f913d3.why: It highlights a manipulation risk for VLM agents that interpret social media, relevant to anyone deploying agents on untrusted content.

sdedee37d8b.title: From Models to Services: Systematizing Security Assurance for Model-as-a-Service
sdedee37d8b.description: arXiv:2611.34623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models are mainly delivered as cloud services, in which the assets of different principals are coupled within a single service pipeline, while the related security research is scattered across several fields with differing threat models. This paper systematizes this research from a service perspective. We decompose Model-as-a-Service (MaaS) into a five-layer stack and five trust boundaries, define six adversary classes and six security goals, use them to code 120 studies, and evaluate 50 defenses under a unified set of criteria. The results show that 44.2% of the studies concentrate on behavioral integrity, while service integrity, availability and cost, and accountability together account for only 13.3%. Defenses are evaluat
sdedee37d8b.summary: A paper systematizes security research for Model-as-a-Service, decomposing it into five layers and trust boundaries and evaluating 50 defenses across 120 studies.
sdedee37d8b.why: It offers a structured threat model for teams securing cloud-hosted LLM services and choosing defenses.

sebbeb8961e.title: DecisionReplay: A Corpus and Offline Simulator for Ensembling Decision Models
sebbeb8961e.description: arXiv:2611.34627v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Comparing ensembles, routers and cascades requires the output of every model on every item, and its cost. Stored collections built for routing keep no per-option probabilities. We provide a dataset on which ensemble methods, routers and cascades are simulated quickly, without new model calls. DecisionReplay holds the probability vectors of 17 commercial decision models, endpoints that return a probability for every answer option, on 35 benchmarks, with the token counts, billed cost and measured latency of every call, all released. sebbeb8961e.summary: DecisionReplay releases a corpus of probability vectors from 17 commercial decision models across 35 benchmarks, with cost and latency data, for offline simulation.
sebbeb8961e.why: Engineers can simulate ensembles, routers, and cascades offline without new model calls, cutting evaluation cost.

sf85e4c385f.title: LatentRL-QAS: Transfer via Latent Reinforcement Learning for Quantum Architecture Search
sf85e4c385f.description: arXiv:2611.34634v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) emerges as a prominent approach to quantum architecture search (QAS), the automated design of quantum circuits. However, transferring what an agent has learned from one number of qubits to another is still weakly explored: the state, the action space and the neural network of a state-of-the-art RL-QAS agent all grow with the number of qubits, which makes transfer learning across qubit counts prohibitive. We make this transfer possible by introducing LatentRL-QAS, a latent space transfer and refresh framework for RL-based QAS. sf85e4c385f.summary: Researchers introduced LatentRL-QAS, a latent-space framework that lets reinforcement learning agents for quantum architecture search transfer learning across different qubit counts.
sf85e4c385f.why: Transfer across qubit counts could cut the cost of automated quantum circuit design, though the impact is limited to quantum computing research.

s5a23c7b4b6.title: Carrying Feature Ablations Across Sparse Autoencoder Seeds
s5a23c7b4b6.description: arXiv:2611.34637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A vision encoder turns an image into one vector per patch, refined layer by layer. A sparse autoencoder (SAE) writes each vector of one layer as a sum of learned directions, most with a coefficient of zero. Researchers call each direction a feature and edit the encoder by removing one feature. An SAE trained from another random seed learns different features. Earlier work matches the two SAEs' features one to one by how closely their directions agree. s5a23c7b4b6.summary: Researchers study how to carry feature ablations from one sparse autoencoder trained with a given random seed to another, since SAEs with different seeds learn different features.
s5a23c7b4b6.why: Feature matching across SAE seeds affects whether interpretability edits to vision encoders transfer reliably, which matters for model editing workflows.

sdfbbf95c62.title: Motion Beyond Pixels: Learning Future Visual Representations for Object-Centric Dynamics
sdfbbf95c62.description: arXiv:2611.34644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many embodied world models predict future states in latent spaces optimized for RGB reconstruction, which do not explicitly prioritize object-level semantics and geometry relevant to motion generation. We present MotionRep, a visual representation world model that jointly generates future DINO representations and 3D object flow, coupling semantic and geometric information with object-centric dynamics. To make high-dimensional DINO features amenable to generative modeling, we introduce DINO-VAE, which combines temporal and channel compression with latent regularization to produce compact latents while preserving semantic and geometric information. sdfbbf95c62.summary: Researchers present MotionRep, a world model that jointly predicts future DINO visual representations and 3D object flow for object-centric dynamics in embodied settings.
sdfbbf95c62.why: Predicting semantic and geometric features rather than raw RGB may help robots plan motion, though the text gives little on practical deployment.

sb9fae07814.title: Do We Still Need Reinforcement Learning When We Can Read the World Model?
sb9fae07814.description: arXiv:2611.34656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning has achieved remarkable success in sequential decision-making, but learning effective policies often requires substantial interaction experience. Model-based reinforcement learning alleviates this dependence by leveraging world models, which are typically used to support planning or policy optimization. In this paper, we investigate an alternative paradigm in which autonomous LLM-based coding agents directly synthesize control policies by reasoning over readable world models. By examining environment source code, these agents translate environmental knowledge into executable decision rules and iteratively refine their policies using online feedback or offline data, without task-specific RL training. sb9fae07814.summary: The paper explores having LLM-based coding agents write control policies directly by reasoning over readable world models and environment source code, bypassing conventional reinforcement learning.
sb9fae07814.why: If coding agents can derive policies from readable world models, teams could reduce interaction data needs, but the text gives limited evidence of performance.

s4f25bdf364.title: Multi-Party Authorization of Maintenance Prescriptions on a Permissioned Blockchain
s4f25bdf364.description: arXiv:2611.34662v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In industrial prescriptive maintenance, an equipment supplier's model may recommend an intervention that a plant schedules, a contractor executes, and a quality or safety function approves. A shared ledger records who submitted the prescription, yet cannot check whether the agreed model and decision rule produced it. We require permissioned-blockchain endorsers to verify a succinct proof of that calculation before releasing a work order. On a four-organization Hyperledger Fabric testbed using a public engine benchmark, this stopped all nine contested or mis-operated prescriptions, whereas hash checks accepted four that either raised simulated maintenance cost or reintroduced late failures.
s4f25bdf364.summary: Researchers propose requiring permissioned-blockchain endorsers to verify succinct proofs of model calculations before approving maintenance prescriptions, tested on a four-organization Hyperledger Fabric setup.
s4f25bdf364.why: Verifiable proofs could let multi-party industrial workflows confirm that recommendations actually came from the agreed model and decision rule.

saa05e66da8.title: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
saa05e66da8.description: arXiv:2611.34671v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling robot learning requires demonstrations that combine realistic visual observations with reliable action supervision. Simulation-based synthesis faces a substantial visual gap relative to real environments, while video-only generation struggles to maintain physically consistent interactions and provide aligned action labels. We present DemoFoundry, an automated framework that couples coding agents with generative rendering to synthesize photorealistic and physically grounded robot demonstrations. Coding agents both construct aligned real--proxy video pairs from existing robot episodes to train a video renderer and write executable interaction programs to generate new demonstrations. saa05e66da8.summary: DemoFoundry couples coding agents with generative rendering to automatically synthesize photorealistic, physically grounded robot demonstrations with aligned action labels.
saa05e66da8.why: Automated generation of realistic robot training data could reduce the cost of scaling robot learning beyond human demonstrations.

s397e5bf7d9.title: RoboEvo$^2$: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution
s397e5bf7d9.description: arXiv:2611.34675v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robots should adapt to unfamiliar environments and acquire new skills through interaction, then execute those skills efficiently with practice. Vision-language-action policies provide efficient control, but often need additional human demonstrations to handle unfamiliar settings; reasoning agents can discover solutions using broad prior knowledge and robot-control APIs, but repeated deliberation and repair are costly. Inspired by human learning through reasoning and practice, we propose RoboEvo$^2$, a framework for recursive harness-policy co-evolution. s397e5bf7d9.summary: RoboEvo² proposes a framework where robot reasoning agents and vision-language-action policies co-evolve recursively, so robots improve skills through interaction and practice.
s397e5bf7d9.why: Co-evolving reasoning agents and control policies could reduce reliance on human demonstrations for robots in unfamiliar settings.

s2f3fc3de1f.title: Find the Clue, Not the Scene: Rethinking Reasoning for Entity Recognition in Vision-Language Models
s2f3fc3de1f.description: arXiv:2611.34681v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Answering a knowledge-based visual question requires first recognizing the entity in the image and then recalling knowledge about it. Thinking vision-language models (VLMs) reason for thousands of tokens before answering, yet it remains underexplored how well such thinking VLMs perform each of these two steps. We therefore analyze thinking VLMs on this task and make two key observations. (1) Recognition is the bottleneck, since 76.3% of errors across four models on ViQuAE stem from misrecognizing the entity, and 84.9% of these failures are resolved once the entity name is provided in the question. s2f3fc3de1f.summary: Analysis of thinking vision-language models finds that entity recognition is the main bottleneck in knowledge-based visual question answering, accounting for 76.3% of errors.
s2f3fc3de1f.why: Recognition, not reasoning, drives most errors, suggesting teams should focus on visual grounding when building VLM-based QA systems.

s7bb39f3924.title: Evacuation Traffic Prediction for Dynamic Transportation Networks over Multiple Hurricanes: A Generalized Graph Learning Approach
s7bb39f3924.description: arXiv:2611.34687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High traffic demand during hurricane evacuations causes severe congestion on major highways, leading to delays and safety risks for evacuees. Predicting evacuation traffic in real-time can significantly enhance evacuation management efforts. However, evacuation traffic is highly dynamic and uncertain due to evolving hurricane characteristics and diverse population response. Each hurricane has unique characteristics and evacuation contexts, resulting in different spatial-temporal traffic patterns. Moreover, the structure of detector-based transportation networks varies across multiple hurricanes. Hence, a model trained on the data from one hurricane may not generalize well for others. s7bb39f3924.summary: Researchers propose a generalized graph learning approach to predict evacuation traffic on highways across multiple hurricanes using detector-based transportation network data.
s7bb39f3924.why: The text gives limited detail on results, so its relevance for engineers is unclear beyond transportation forecasting use cases.

sd8155ccb00.title: Maco-RL: Scaling Agent Capabilities with Mixed-Task Reinforcement Learning
sd8155ccb00.description: arXiv:2611.34703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mixed-task reinforcement learning (MixRL) directly trains a unified policy across domains to continually expand agent capabilities without training separate specialists or requiring an extra distillation stage. Despite its appeal, scaling MixRL poses significant challenges in achieving stable and efficient mixed-task learning, effectively allocating rollout compute, and supporting continual domain expansion. To address these challenges, we propose Maco-RL, an approach that effectively scales MixRL. sd8155ccb00.why: Training one policy across multiple task domains without separate specialists or distillation could simplify agent training pipelines.

sd53ed3dac4.title: When the Proxy Is Wrong: Mismatch-Corrected Bandits for Adaptive Data Sampling
sd53ed3dac4.description: arXiv:2611.34707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data allocation methods often use a small proxy model to select training data for a larger target model. However, this proxy can rank data differently from the target, leading to suboptimal training performance. To address this problem, we model the mismatch between the proxy and target models and incorporate it into the allocation decision. To do so, the problem is cast as a multi-fidelity bandit, where each arm is a data intervention. sd53ed3dac4.summary: Researchers model the mismatch between small proxy models and larger target models as a multi-fidelity bandit for adaptive training data selection.
sd53ed3dac4.why: Correcting for proxy-target ranking mismatch could improve data selection efficiency when small models guide training of larger ones.

s259547581b.title: How Well Do Vision-Language Scene Graphs Serve as Memory for Embodied Question Answering?
s259547581b.description: arXiv:2611.34745v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Embodied QA needs memory, but answer accuracy mixes retained evidence, reading errors and question priors. For a simulated multi-room scene-graph pipeline we define answerability: the fraction of questions a fixed rule-based reader answers correctly from the graph alone. The baseline recovers 24.1% of visible object types and its room labels flicker. Four targeted repairs double recall, raise answerability from 27.2% to 37.4%, and improve retrained QA from 71.4% to 75.9%, yet better object F1 can lower answerability. A question-type prior beats this reader on every predicted graph. In one real-video test, graph memory lowers accuracy. These exploratory findings favour scoring retained evidence alongside accuracy.

s259547581b.why: Better object recall does not always improve answerability, so teams building graph-based memory should measure answer utility directly.

s77ac846f97.title: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Adaptive and Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
s77ac846f97.description: arXiv:2611.34756v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fully online on-policy distillation (OPD) is costly for long-horizon agents because each update depends on fresh environment rollouts. Prefix replay offers an efficient alternative by sampling current-student responses from stored histories, reducing idle time for long-tail rollouts and allowing each collected trajectory to support multiple updates. However, our analysis of the complete prefix replay pipeline identifies two limitations in long-horizon settings. s77ac846f97.summary: Researchers propose an adaptive method for on-policy distillation in long-horizon agents that reuses stored prefix histories to reduce costly fresh environment rollouts.
s77ac846f97.why: Reducing rollout costs for long-horizon agent training could make distillation practical for teams with limited environment compute.

sc90513705f.title: Reading Fine-Tuning Diffs Through Lenses: Model Diffing for Backdoor Detection
sc90513705f.description: arXiv:2611.34758v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a common scoring system based on token readouts to evaluate weight, activation and output-based model diffing methods for backdoor detection in fine-tuning processes. sc90513705f.summary: Researchers introduce a scoring system based on token readouts to compare weight, activation, and output-based model diffing methods for detecting backdoors in fine-tuned models.
sc90513705f.why: Standardized comparison of diffing methods gives security teams a clearer basis for checking whether fine-tuning introduced a backdoor.

s2afc837aa8.title: One Model, Many Modes: Evolving System Prompt Ensembles for Creative Generation
s2afc837aa8.description: arXiv:2611.34760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Preference-aligned LLMs can exhibit mode collapse, concentrating their output distributions around a narrow set of high-reward responses. This limits creative generation, which requires quality, novelty, and diversity. Existing test-time methods often emphasize diversity, giving less attention to whether individual responses are both high-quality and novel. This distinction matters in practical use, where users may seek a single compelling, original response. We formalize creative generation as a multi-objective distributional optimization problem and introduce SEPO, a training-free framework for System Prompt Ensemble Optimization. The framework combines prompt evolution with greedy max-min selection to identify behaviorally distinct syste
s2afc837aa8.summary: Researchers formalize creative generation as a multi-objective optimization and propose evolving system prompt ensembles to produce responses that are both high-quality and novel.
s2afc837aa8.why: Ensembles of system prompts could help teams counter mode collapse in aligned LLMs when they need diverse, original outputs.

s73fa4f721e.title: InterConRank: Joint Node Centrality in Interconnected Heterogeneous Networks
s73fa4f721e.description: arXiv:2611.34763v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two nodes with identical connections within their own layer can differ in importance if their neighbors in another layer occupy different positions in the network. We introduce InterConRank, a centrality algorithm that computes a separate node ranking for each layer of an interconnected network. Directed dependencies specify which layers supply scores to each receiving layer. InterConRank normalizes each type of link separately and updates all layers together, so a score can cross into a layer in one iteration and propagate along its internal links in the next. s73fa4f721e.summary: Researchers introduce InterConRank, a centrality algorithm that ranks nodes separately in each layer of interconnected heterogeneous networks, letting cross-layer neighbors shift scores.
s73fa4f721e.why: Offers a way to rank node importance in multi-layer graphs where same-layer connections alone miss cross-layer influence.

sedfbdcb3eb.title: Make the Adversary Spend More: Stateful Deception as a Cost-Exchange Primitive for AI-Era Cyber Defense
sedfbdcb3eb.description: arXiv:2611.34770v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are transforming the economics of intrusion by reducing the attacker's cost to scan and adapt, while tempting defenders into unbounded compute. We argue that cyber deception should be judged by the cost exchange it imposes, not by realism or detection, and that the primitive making that exchange favorable is adversary-specific persistent state. Rather than a honeypot that resets or merges sessions, each recognized adversary re-enters the world it believes it has compromised, kept coherent with its own past actions and isolated from every other adversary, while the language model acts only as a constrained renderer of explicit state, never as its store. We formalize the trade-off as a Deception Exchange Rate (DER
sedfbdcb3eb.summary: Researchers propose stateful cyber deception that keeps each recognized adversary in a persistent, coherent fake environment to raise attackers' costs.
sedfbdcb3eb.why: Suggests defenders can judge deception by cost imposed on LLM-enabled attackers rather than realism or detection rates.

s73a6964aff.title: When Every Rollout Fails: Splicing Learner-Conditioned Options into Long-Horizon Agent RL
s73a6964aff.description: arXiv:2611.34777v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Group-based reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards often yields all-fail groups on long-horizon agent tasks: every sampled trajectory receives zero reward, leaving group-relative methods without a reward-based policy gradient. A common remedy supplies complete solutions from a stronger model, but full trajectories are expensive and expose the learner to long off-policy histories. We introduce SPLICE, which constructs local training targets from failed current-policy trajectories online. For each all-fail group, a proposal model selects a splice point in a current-policy trajectory and generates several bounded options from that point. We estimate each option's value using repeated current-policy continuations, convert positive estim
s73a6964aff.summary: SPLICE constructs local training targets from failed policy trajectories online, helping group-based RL on long-horizon agent tasks where every rollout fails.
s73a6964aff.why: Addresses zero-gradient failure in RL for long-horizon agents without relying on expensive full expert trajectories.

s489801fe9a.title: PersonaFactory: Stylistic User Prompt Augmentation with Synthetic Persona Bank
s489801fe9a.description: arXiv:2611.34785v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models increasingly replace real people in the AI development pipeline, as they are used to generate training dialogues at scale and to drive alignment and evaluation. However, out-of-the-box models produce monolingual and stylistically flat texts as synthetic user prompts, failing to replicate the real user-AI communication mechanics. We present PersonaFactory, an end-to-end pipeline that generates detailed user personas and uses them to augment existing user prompts from their point of view, producing a bank of over 740000 structured synthetic personas detailing their background and communication behaviors, and a corpus of roughly 1.24 million persona-styled synthetic conversations spanning 85 languages. We evaluate the eff
s489801fe9a.summary: PersonaFactory is a pipeline that generates synthetic user personas to augment prompts, producing a bank of over 740,000 stylistically varied user prompts.
s489801fe9a.why: Could improve synthetic training and evaluation data that currently sounds monolingual and stylistically flat.

s1e213fee8e.title: HOG-WAM: Improving Visual Robustness through Future Gradient Prediction
s1e213fee8e.description: arXiv:2611.34811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet visual corruption can disrupt the resulting policies. We introduce HOG-WAM, which adds future Histograms of Oriented Gradients (HOG) as structural supervision derived directly from demonstration images. An auxiliary HOG diffusion transformer (DiT) module reads RGB features through asymmetric attention, allowing its objective to shape the visual representation used for control. The module is used only during training and removed at inference, preserving FastWAM's RGB-to-action architecture. s1e213fee8e.summary: HOG-WAM adds future Histograms of Oriented Gradients as training-only supervision to world-action models to improve policy robustness against visual corruption.
s1e213fee8e.why: Offers a training-time fix for robot policies failing under visual corruption, with no added inference cost.

s86b16d1b32.title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models
s86b16d1b32.description: arXiv:2611.34813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video generation models are increasingly evaluated as visual reasoners: given a first frame and a natural-language prompt, can the model produce the video in which the specified task is carried out? The paradigm is considered advantageous because the reasoning is native to the visual medium, unfolding directly in the frames rather than through language or code. Whether this native route is in fact the more reliable path to visual reasoning has not been tested against a symbolic alternative under the same conditions. s86b16d1b32.summary: A study compares coding agents against video generation models on visual reasoning tasks under matched conditions, finding code-based solving stronger.
s86b16d1b32.why: Suggests symbolic code execution may be more reliable than video generation for visual reasoning tasks.

s647e74c303.title: Transferring Architecture as an Optimization Prior
s647e74c303.description: arXiv:2611.34816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Initialization determines the optimization "fate" of a model, going far beyond just setting the scale of its weights. It establishes a fundamental initial geometry over the input data, dictating certain aspects such as which examples are considered close and which representations gradient descent will naturally refine first. In this paper, we view the initial geometry of a network as an optimization prior and ask whether a network can change its optimization prior by referencing a completely different architecture. To investigate this question, we use an initialization procedure where a target network is aligned to the representational geometry of a randomly initialized guide network before any downstream training occurs. s647e74c303.summary: The paper investigates whether a network can change its optimization prior by referencing a different architecture during initialization.
s647e74c303.why: Explores how initialization geometry shapes training, a question relevant to model design and training efficiency.

sb9c51e53f2.title: Not all world models can doubt: how training objective and architecture shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models
sb9c51e53f2.description: arXiv:2611.34830v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World models predict how an environment responds to actions, so that candidate actions can be evaluated before execution. Executed actions, or decisions, taken in this manner are only as reliable as the model's predictive capabilities, and predictions in turn are only reliable within the model's experience. Epistemic uncertainty (EU) is the signal that marks where that experience ends. In this work we offer an extensive empirical study on how training objectives and architectures shape epistemic uncertainty of world models.
